papers.title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Verifier-Based RL Beyond Supervised Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) is usually evaluated as an alternative to supervised fine-tuning (SFT), or as a stage that follows it, with the implicit assumption that the RL stage contributes gains of its own. We measure that contribution directly, in a controlled setting where both stages can be run to completion and compared exactly. We built gpu-train-debug, a deterministic benchmark of 1,877 synthetic GPU and LLM training failure diagnosis tasks across 30 archetypes, graded by a programmatic verifier with partial credit, and calibrated so that a mid-tier model scores in a 0.60 to 0.75 band. A pilot produced a surprise: 1,200 gold demonstrations nearly solved the benchmark (SFT 0.785 on the hard split), while 15 steps of GRPO from the base model did not move it (0.314 vs 0.311 base). We therefore amended the study, in writing and before the full run, to ask the sharper question: what does verifier-based RL add beyond demonstrations? At the pre-registered scale (60 GRPO steps, learning rate 1e-6), the answer is: no detectable improvement in-distribution (+0.22 points, 95% CI [-0.06, +0.51]), and a modest but measurable improvement under distribution shift (+0.33 points on a held-out OOD split, CI [+0.02, +0.68]). SFT accounted for most of the available improvement, while verifier-based RL produced only modest additional gains under distribution shift. The residual errors SFT leaves are mostly systematic, identical across samples, which likely reduces the within-group learning signal available to GRPO. A full 60-step cold-start GRPO arm confirms the pilot at the full horizon. The whole study cost $8.69 of compute and is fully reproducible from archived generations, frozen configs, and tagged code.

translation.abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) is usually evaluated as an alternative to supervised fine-tuning (SFT), or as a stage that follows it, with the implicit assumption that the RL stage contributes gains of its own. We built gpu-train-debug, a deterministic benchmark of 1,877 synthetic GPU and LLM training failure diagnosis tasks across 30 archetypes, graded by a programmatic verifier with partial credit, and calibrated so that a mid-tier model scores in a 0.60 to 0.75 band. A pilot produced a surprise: 1,200 gold demonstrations nearly solved the benchmark (SFT 0.785 on the hard split), while 15 steps of GRPO from the base model did not move it (0.314 vs 0.311 base). We therefore amended the study, in writing and before the full run, to ask the sharper question: what does verifier-based RL add beyond demonstrations? At the pre-registered scale (60 GRPO steps, learning rate 1e-6), the answer is: no detectable improvement in-distribution (+0.22 points, 95% CI [-0.06, +0.51]), and a modest but measurable improvement under distribution shift (+0.33 points on a held-out OOD split, CI [+0.02, +0.68]). SFT accounted for most of the available improvement, while verifier-based RL produced only modest additional gains under distribution shift. The residual errors SFT leaves are mostly systematic, identical across samples, which likely reduces the within-group learning signal available to GRPO. A full 60-step cold-start GRPO arm confirms the pilot at the full horizon. The whole study cost $8.69 of compute and is fully reproducible from archived generations, frozen configs, and tagged code.

papers.title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
papers.abstract: Indirect prompt-injection (IPI) benchmarks predominantly test planted instructions that redirect a tool-using agent toward an attacker-chosen task. Yet attacker-controlled content can instead tamper with the outcome of the task already in progress. A buyer's dispute evidence can cite a false refund policy to inflate a refund without changing the task. We define IPI by authority rather than instruction-like wording: planted content constitutes an attack when it attempts to influence a decision that its source is not authorized to determine. We introduce a benchmark that makes this boundary explicit: in each of 90 validated cases across three tool-use environments, the user request specifies the source that resolves the targeted decision. Every attack tampers with a decision required by the benign task rather than replacing that task. Each case has attacks with the same harmful outcome that target up to six parts of the agent's decision making: its objective, decision rules, available actions, expected consequences, reading of observations, or beliefs about the current state. Without a defense, attacks on three of the five other targets (decision rules, available actions, and state) have higher mean success than objective attacks across five LLMs. A detection-and-removal defense reduces objective-targeting attacks to 2.4% success but leaves observation- and state-targeting attacks at 9.5% and 12.1%; this gap persists under detection-optimized rewrites. A tool-policy defense still allows 15.4% attack success, close to 17.0% without a defense, because these attacks generally retain expected tools and manipulate values obtained during execution. Evaluations whose attacks redirect the task or target only the agent's objective can therefore overestimate the coverage of these defenses. Code and data are available at this https URL.

papers.title: What the Middleman Delivers: Answer Behavior, Tool Permissions, and Billed Usage in LLM API Relays
papers.abstract: Third-party application programming interface (API) relays offer access to large language models (LLMs), often at lower prices. Users depend on these services for model quality, instruction compliance, and accurate billing. However, existing studies leave unclear whether relays meet these expectations together. We test 20 relays offering GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5. First, we compare answers to knowledge questions with batch-matched official responses. In our first-round sample, the analysis flags 7/10 low-price and 2/10 same- or higher-price relays for behavioral differences. On retesting 35 pairs, seven gain or lose a flag under the original rules, and six under matched correction families. Because answer comparisons cannot reveal every delivery problem, we examine returned content and tool permissions. No injection is confirmed in 3,332 screened responses to a fixed, non-adversarial code and setup workload, yet four relays return tool calls despite instructions disabling them in the first round. Finally, to connect reported usage to actual costs, we compare input-token counts with official references and check balances. For identical requests, five relays report 4,200 to 60,000 more input tokens than the official API. Where balances are available (six services), charges follow reported usage at listed prices, including extra reported input tokens at one service. Our study shows that advertised models and prices are insufficient to judge relay reliability. It identifies unexplained billed token quantities and tool-permission violations as risks and shows why service evaluations need repeated measurements.

papers.title: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Drug discovery requires continuous scientific decision-making across a vast research space. We introduce PharmAgents2, an autonomous system for end-to-end drug discovery that combines knowledge-enhanced decision-making with organized large-scale exploration. Paper2Skill extracts transferable scientific decision knowledge from public sources and, together with expert-developed skills, supports research decisions. Self-Scaling Discovery expands exploration through parallel agents inheriting research context and decision-making capabilities across targets, scientific hypotheses, and discovery strategies. We introduce PharmAgents-Bench v0.1, comprising 121 questions across nine decision scenarios and three end-to-end tasks assessed with expert-defined process rubrics. PharmAgents2 outperforms evaluated baselines in most decision categories and achieves the highest process scores on all three end-to-end tasks. In three real-world studies, autonomous investigations generated findings subsequently supported by human-executed experiments. For LpxH, PharmAgents2 hypothesized a previously unreported allosteric site and screened compounds against it, identifying a novel inhibitor scaffold with experimentally confirmed inhibitory activity and binding. For JAK1, it prioritized a covalent inhibition strategy and nominated compounds with experimentally demonstrated activity. Starting from a known bioactive molecule, Self-Scaling Discovery explored candidate targets across the proteome and identified a new binding target, with the interaction subsequently confirmed experimentally. PharmAgents2 represents a prototype of a virtual pharmaceutical company, marking a step toward autonomous end-to-end drug discovery.

papers.title: Who Should Know What? Empirical Information Design for Multi-Agent LLM Economies
papers.abstract: The performance of multi-agent LLM systems depends not only on the capabilities of the underlying models but also on information-sharing policies, which govern what information each agent observes and at what level of detail. But does providing AI agents with more detailed information always improve collective outcomes, or can transparency paradoxically degrade efficiency? To investigate this, we introduce empirical information design, an experimental framework that systematically compares disclosure policies across economic markets populated by LLM agents, while holding interaction rules and models fixed. We evaluate ten frontier LLMs in multi-resource trade, bilateral bargaining, and double auctions, using ground-truth utilities to decouple identified opportunities from realized outcomes. We find that finer information disclosure yields highly model-dependent results. In trade, revealing exact valuations rather than ordinal preference rankings reduces realized gains for GPT-6 Sol (from 98% to 91% of maximum) yet increases them for Claude Sonnet 5 (from 72% to 86%). In bargaining, exact information leads Grok 4.7 to produce less balanced agreements, whereas Claude Opus 5.5 divides gains symmetrically. In double auctions, full disclosure inflates price demands, triggering market breakdown and lowering welfare for Gemini 3.1 Pro (97% to 78%), Claude Opus 5.5 (94% to 64%), and Grok 4.7 (97% to 62%). Overall, these results suggest that model selection and information design must be co-optimized, as LLMs vary in how their strategic responses to information impact system objectives.

papers.title: An Information Bottleneck for Post-hoc Memorization Mitigation in LLMs
papers.abstract: Recent studies have shown that large language models (LLMs) can memorize and reproduce copyrighted training data, raising serious privacy and intellectual property concerns. In this work, we investigate whether memorization can be mitigated without modifying or retraining the underlying model through an information bottleneck. We propose a modular plug-and-play framework that inserts a nonparametric variational information bottleneck (NVIB) between a frozen LLM backbone and its language modeling head. By compressing the final hidden representations before token prediction, the proposed bottleneck aims to preserve general linguistic knowledge while filtering out highly specific memorized sequences. We evaluate our approach on memorization extraction tasks involving book passages and on standard language modeling benchmarks to measure the trade-off between memorization reduction and downstream utility. Our experiments show that the NVIB layer substantially reduces extractability while maintaining competitive performance on benchmark tasks. These results suggest that adding an information bottleneck offers a practical and architecture agnostic direction for post-hoc memorization mitigation in pretrained LLMs.

papers.title: ReferClaw: Disambiguating User Intent for Egocentric Assistance
papers.abstract: Users of egocentric AI assistants often ask short, ambiguous questions whose intended referents cannot be uniquely resolved from video and dialogue history. For example, "Where did I leave it?" may refer to several previously handled objects. Existing VideoQA systems typically commit to a single interpretation, risking plausible but intention-misaligned answers. We introduce ReferClaw, an agentic framework that formulates egocentric streaming QA as an interactive process: the assistant asks clarifying questions to resolve user intent before answering. Three cooperating agents identify candidate interpretations, request clarification, and generate answers grounded in the resolved intent and visual evidence. A bounded, cost-aware policy balances expected information gain against user effort while limiting clarification turns and question complexity. Referclaw learns from interaction through intent-specific skill updates and process-reward-guided policy optimization with agent-level credit assignment. Evaluations on augmented egocentric QA benchmarks demonstrate improved answer accuracy and joint answer-and-grounding performance over existing baselines, alongside zero-shot transfer across datasets. These findings support interactive clarification as a practical approach to resolving online user intent in egocentric streaming assistance.

papers.title: MCPHallu: Benchmarking Reasoning, Execution, and Memory Hallucinations in MCP Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which allows them to discover and invoke tools across multiple servers at runtime. Existing MCP benchmarks primarily measure task completion; where they diagnose failures, they do so after execution rather than building specific reasoning, execution, and memory failure risks into task construction. We introduce MCPHallu, a benchmark for diagnosing hallucination-prone agent failures in MCP environments along three axes: reasoning, execution, and memory. MCPHallu contains 358 tasks across five capability domains and runs on 36 production MCP servers in isolated containers. Each task is designed with a structural trigger that makes one of four subtypes the dominant failure risk: Branch Collapse, Unreachable Goal, Tool Misuse, or Context Forgetting. This design enables subtype-level analysis rather than aggregate task success alone. We evaluate fourteen frontier LLM agents from eight vendors on 5{,}012 trajectories. Current MCP agents remain vulnerable to hallucination-inducing tool environments, achieving an average score of 0.642 on a $[0,1]$ scale (higher is better). Failures concentrate on Unreachable Goal tasks, where the average score drops to 0.458 and 23.2\% of runs pass, indicating that agents often continue issuing tool calls or claim successful completion rather than recognizing infeasible goals. Subtype rankings diverge sharply: a model's rank shifts by 6.9 of 13 positions on average across subtypes, and Branch Collapse is uncorrelated with Unreachable Goal across models ($r = -0.12$). MCPHallu is released at this https URL.

papers.title: Distributed Optimization Involving Non-Lipschitzian, Linear Composite Functions: Unified Algorithm Design and Convergence Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper formulates a generic distributed nonsmooth optimization problem subject to edge-based equality constraints, local inequality constraints characterized by general convex functions, as well as globally coupling constraints including affine equality and nonlinear inequality. The terminal goal is to minimize the sum of local non-differentiable convex functions and proximable nonsmooth convex composite terms attached to linear operators, over networked multi-agent systems. This formulated framework not only applies in complex practical problems but also reduces to existing distributed optimization structures. To cope with technical issues caused by local linear mappings, potential multiple nonsmooth functions and coupling nonlinear constraints, we first derive a new local first-order condition, and further present a novel fully distributed optimization algorithm based on variable decompositions and proximal operators. Specifically, the proposed algorithm allows each agent to update states via local information exchange and through {locally fixed step-sizes}, and to find inexact solutions of subproblems without loss of convergence speed. In contrast to existing tailor-made algorithms for the bounded gradients of objective functions or affine constraints, our algorithm is capable of solving more practical cases involving general convex functions and nonlinear constraints. Under mild assumptions, the convergence rate $o(1/k)$ in terms of the optimality and successive-difference metrics is achieved, by constructing the equivalent variational inequalities of the proposed algorithm. Finally, numerical experiments on practical application problems illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: CAMP: Context-Aware Mapping and Placement for LLMs on 3D-IMC Arrays
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) incur severe memory-access overheads due to the cost of loading large weight matrices and key-value (KV) caches. Analog In-Memory Computing (AIMC) is an emerging solution that enables computation directly on static weights stored in memory, substantially reducing energy and latency. 3D-IMC further stacks memory arrays into vertical tiers, increasing capacity but revealing a new challenge: how weights are placed in memory determines which matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) can execute concurrently, affecting latency and throughput. The concurrency aspect of 3D-IMC weight-mapping remains underexplored in the literature, leading to sub-optimal utilization of compute resources on 3D-IMC chips. In this context we propose CAMP (Context-Aware Mapping and Placement), an inference-context-aware weight mapping algorithm for 3D-IMC-based LLM accelerators. CAMP captures the potential resource contention resulting from the architecture, targeted network, and runtime context in a conflict matrix, enabling throughput-optimized weight mapping. This mapping is refined through a profiling-driven feedback loop that efficiently prunes the search space and returns optimized mappings within practical runtimes. CAMP is an offline, software-based solution requiring no hardware changes and improving 3D-IMC compute utilization from 42.4% to 60.3%, delivering up to 2.0x higher 3D-IMC throughput and 1.74x higher end-to-end throughput over state-of-the-art mapping algorithms.

translation.title: CAMP：面向3D-IMC阵列上LLM的上下文感知映射与放置
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）因加载大型权重矩阵和键值（KV）缓存而产生严重的内存访问开销。模拟存内计算（AIMC）是一种新兴解决方案，可直接对存储在内存中的静态权重进行计算，大幅降低能耗和延迟。3D-IMC进一步将内存阵列垂直堆叠为多层，增加了容量，但也带来了新挑战：权重在内存中的放置方式决定了哪些矩阵向量乘法（MVM）可以并发执行，从而影响延迟和吞吐量。3D-IMC权重映射的并发性问题在文献中仍缺乏研究，导致3D-IMC芯片计算资源利用率欠佳。为此，我们提出CAMP（Context-Aware Mapping and Placement），一种面向基于3D-IMC的LLM加速器的推理上下文感知权重映射算法。CAMP将架构、目标网络和运行时上下文导致的潜在资源竞争捕获到冲突矩阵中，实现吞吐量优化的权重映射。该映射通过一个基于性能剖析的反馈回路进行细化，高效剪枝搜索空间，并在实际可接受的运行时间内返回优化映射。CAMP是一种离线、纯软件的解决方案，无需硬件改动，将3D-IMC计算利用率从42.4%提升至60.3%，相比最先进的映射算法，3D-IMC吞吐量最高提升2.0倍，端到端吞吐量最高提升1.74倍。
translation.brief: 解决3D-IMC芯片上权重放置导致的MVM并发受限问题，提出上下文感知的权重映射算法CAMP，通过冲突矩阵和剖析反馈回路优化吞吐量。

papers.title: Evaluating Language Model Features for Zero-Shot Time-Series Anomaly Detection Under Isolation Assumption
papers.abstract: Time-Series Anomaly Detection (TSAD) is a fundamentally challenging task: it is unsupervised, requires high local precision capabilities, and suffers from limited labelled data. Recent work has explored adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) to time-series via cross-modal transfer. However, existing approaches are poorly suited to Multivariate TSAD (MTSAD), as tokenisation often obscures fine-grained temporal and variables structures, and most methods optimise auxiliary objectives such as forecasting or reconstruction. We posit that these surrogate objectives become unreliable as model capacity increases. Highly expressive models risk reconstructing or forecasting anomalies, undermining the foundations of both strategies. Instead, we propose to use LLMs purely as feature extractors and directly analyse their induced feature spaces. In this work, investigate the ability of LLMs to provide useful representations for MTSADs in a zero-shot setting through classification. To this end, we study the separability of the extracted features, under the assumption that anomalous features should be isolated from normal ones. We analyse their temporal and contextual discriminative ability using simple step-wise tokenisation schemes, with one time-step per token, which preserve fine-grained local information. Their usability for MTSAD is assessed using an unsupervised Isolation Forest, enabling a direct evaluation of the resulting representation quality. We further investigate whether the observed performance can be attributed to the language-related pre-training of the LLMs or arises independently of it. Our results provide empirical insight into the ability of LLMs to represent multivariate time-series for anomaly detection and highlight broader applications of cross-modal foundation models.

translation.title: 隔离假设下评估语言模型特征用于零样本时间序列异常检测
translation.abstract: 时间序列异常检测（TSAD）是一项根本性挑战任务：它是无监督的，需要高局部精度能力，且标注数据有限。近期工作探索了通过跨模态迁移将大语言模型（LLM）适配到时间序列。然而，现有方法不太适合多变量TSAD（MTSAD），因为分词往往掩盖了细粒度的时间和变量结构，且大多数方法优化的是预测或重建等辅助目标。我们认为，随着模型容量的增加，这些替代目标变得不可靠。高表达能力的模型可能重建或预测出异常，从而破坏这两种策略的基础。相反，我们提议将LLM纯粹用作特征提取器，并直接分析其诱导的特征空间。在本工作中，我们通过分类研究LLM在零样本设置下为MTSAD提供有用表示的能力。为此，我们在异常特征应与正常特征隔离的假设下，研究提取特征的可分性。我们使用简单的逐步分词方案（每个token对应一个时间步，保留细粒度局部信息）分析其时间和上下文判别能力。使用无监督的Isolation Forest评估其对MTSAD的可用性，从而直接评估所得表示的质量。我们进一步研究观察到的性能是否可归因于LLM的语言相关预训练，还是独立于预训练而产生。我们的结果为LLM表示多变量时间序列用于异常检测的能力提供了实证洞见，并凸显了跨模态基础模型的更广泛应用。
translation.brief: 解决LLM在多变量时间序列异常检测中的表示能力评估问题，将LLM作为纯特征提取器，用逐步分词和Isolation Forest在零样本设置下检验特征可分性。

papers.title: Seeing Beyond the Next Step: World-Model-Guided Human-Like Navigation in Multi-Agent Scenes
papers.abstract: Selecting a next motion in a populated scene is not just a matter of avoiding what is currently in the way: an action can be locally feasible yet drift onto the road instead of the crosswalk, cut into a stream of crossing pedestrians, or bottleneck a narrow passage. These failure modes are invisible from the current state alone, and acting on them requires reasoning about what each candidate action will cause. World models offer exactly this, namely action-conditioned predictions of the future, but rolling them out at every decision step is a cost deployable navigation systems cannot pay, and the field has largely traded foresight for speed. We argue this is a false dichotomy. The natural place for a world model in human-aware navigation is at training time, as a preference oracle that distills foresight into a fast policy, rather than at inference time, as an online planner. We pair a discrete visual action prior with two task-aligned world models, one for nearby social dynamics and one for future scene semantics, that score candidate actions by their predicted consequences and refine the policy through group-relative preference distillation. At deployment, both world models are removed and the policy acts in a single forward pass. Across five held-out evaluation scenarios, this yields navigation that is simultaneously safer, more socially and group-coherent, and more goal-directed than strong reactive and learned baselines, with naive observers rating the resulting motion as more human-like. Taken together, our findings point to a different approach for bringing world-model foresight into deployable agents: not accelerating rollouts, but amortizing them into the policy so that the cost of looking ahead is confined to training. Project page: this https URL

translation.title: 超越下一步：多智能体场景中世界模型引导的类人导航
translation.abstract: 在人群密集场景中选择下一步动作不仅仅是避开当前障碍：一个动作可能在局部可行，却会偏离人行道走上马路、切入过街人流，或堵塞狭窄通道。这些失败模式仅从当前状态无法察觉，对其采取行动需要推理每个候选动作将导致的后果。世界模型恰好提供了这种能力，即动作条件化的未来预测，但在每个决策步骤都进行世界模型推演的代价是可部署导航系统无法承受的，因此该领域大多以牺牲前瞻性换取速度。我们认为这是一个伪二分法。世界模型在以人为本导航中的自然位置是在训练阶段，作为将前瞻性蒸馏到快速策略中的偏好oracle，而非在推理阶段作为在线规划器。我们将离散视觉动作先验与两个任务对齐的世界模型配对，一个用于近邻社交动态，一个用于未来场景语义，它们根据预测后果对候选动作打分，并通过组相对偏好蒸馏优化策略。部署时移除两个世界模型，策略仅需单次前向传播即可行动。在五个留出评估场景中，相比强反应式和 learned 基线，该方法实现了同时更安全、更具社交与群体一致性、更目标导向的导航，且朴素观察者认为其运动更类人。综上，我们的发现为将世界模型前瞻性引入可部署智能体指出了不同路径：不是加速推演，而是将其摊销到策略中，使前瞻的成本仅限于训练阶段。项目页面：this https URL
translation.brief: 解决导航策略缺乏前瞻性导致的社会性失败问题，将世界模型作为训练期偏好oracle，通过组相对偏好蒸馏将前瞻性摊销进单次前向传播的快速策略。

papers.title: Evaluating Token Probabilities as Confidence Estimators in Human Behavior Simulations: A Case Study in Luxembourgish Next Like Prediction
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior, their operational validity is typically assessed through accuracy alone, implicitly treating human behavior as deterministic. We argue that on noisy digital trace data, a model's performance depends not only on predicting the correct outcome but on its calibration. We present a case study testing whether the token probabilities of open-weight LLMs can serve as confidence estimates in a Next Like Prediction task: predicting how a user of the Luxembourgish news platform this http URL rates a comment, conditioned on their prior interactions. Evaluating Ministral 3 (3B, 8B), we find that, with in-context learning only, the tested models are overconfident and are outperformed on accuracy and calibration by a simple statistical baseline. Accuracy and calibration do not move together: scaling from 3B to 8B improves accuracy while degrading calibration, and longer behavioral histories raise accuracy while confidence declines. Task-specific supervised fine-tuning acts as an effective calibration intervention, reducing Expected Calibration Error from 0.2 to 0.006 while improving accuracy from 0.536 to 0.758. We conclude that confidence estimation should be evaluated alongside accuracy to improve validity when using LLM-based agents.

translation.title: 评估token概率作为人类行为模拟中的置信度估计器：卢森堡语Next Like预测案例研究
translation.abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地用于模拟人类行为，其操作有效性通常仅通过准确率评估，隐含地将人类行为视为确定性的。我们认为，在含噪的数字痕迹数据上，模型性能不仅取决于预测正确结果，还取决于其校准程度。我们提出一个案例研究，测试开源权重LLM的token概率能否在Next Like预测任务中作为置信度估计：预测卢森堡新闻平台this http URL的用户在给定其先前交互的条件下如何为评论点赞。通过评估Ministral 3（3B、8B），我们发现仅使用上下文学习时，被测模型过度自信，在准确率和校准上均不如简单的统计基线。准确率与校准并不同步变化：从3B扩展到8B提高了准确率却降低了校准，更长的行为历史提高准确率但置信度下降。任务特定的监督微调是一种有效的校准干预手段，将期望校准误差（ECE）从0.2降至0.006，同时将准确率从0.536提升至0.758。我们得出结论：在使用基于LLM的智能体时，应将置信度估计与准确率一同评估以提升有效性。
translation.brief: 解决LLM模拟人类行为时置信度校准被忽视的问题，以卢森堡语Next Like预测为案例，检验token概率作为置信度估计的有效性及微调的校准作用。

papers.title: Foresee to Trade: Forecast-Augmented Policy Optimization for Portfolio Management
papers.abstract: Online investment services must translate asset opportunities into investment outcomes for users' accounts, yet the same market opportunity can warrant different account actions. We study how supervision from future asset opportunities can strengthen account-level trading decisions and propose Forecast-Augmented Relative Policy Optimization (FRPO). FRPO separately supervises asset opportunities and account decisions through a jointly learned representation: a Financial State Head (FSH) learns future relative-return targets to provide asset-level opportunity supervision, while Same-Path Group-Relative Optimization compares trading trajectories under the same market path and initial account to provide account-level relative-outcome supervision. An Adaptive Gate coordinates auxiliary supervision using predictive variance and gradient alignment. FSH is used only during training; inference uses the encoder and policy for trading. Across DJIA30, TOPIX Core30, and three investment-style portfolios, ten-seed evaluations show that FRPO achieves the highest mean cumulative and annualized returns among the compared methods in all five settings. These results support strengthening investment agents' trading decisions through joint supervision from asset opportunities and trading outcomes.

translation.title: 预见以交易：面向投资组合管理的预测增强策略优化
translation.abstract: 在线投资服务必须将资产机会转化为用户账户的投资结果，然而同一市场机会可能需要不同的账户操作。我们研究来自未来资产机会的监督如何强化账户级交易决策，并提出预测增强相对策略优化（FRPO）。FRPO通过联合学习的表示分别监督资产机会和账户决策：金融状态头（FSH）学习未来相对收益目标以提供资产级机会监督，而Same-Path Group-Relative Optimization在相同市场路径和初始账户下比较交易轨迹，以提供账户级相对结果监督。自适应门（Adaptive Gate）利用预测方差和梯度对齐来协调辅助监督。FSH仅在训练期间使用；推理时使用编码器和策略进行交易。在DJIA30、TOPIX Core30和三个投资风格组合上，十种子评估表明FRPO在所有五个设置中均取得所比较方法中最高的平均累计和年化收益。这些结果支持通过资产机会和交易结果的联合监督来强化投资智能体的交易决策。
translation.brief: 解决账户级交易决策缺乏对未来资产机会监督的问题，提出FRPO，通过金融状态头和同路径组相对优化实现资产机会与交易结果的联合监督。

papers.title: Uncovering Systematic Blind Spots in Graph Database Testing through Integration and Process-Level Analysis
papers.abstract: Graph databases are becoming foundational infrastructure for connected data, and a growing body of automated testing techniques has uncovered many bugs across mature graph database systems. Each technique checks a different aspect of correctness and exposes a different class of defect. Combining them is the natural next step, but each technique is judged by the real bugs it finds, not by useless reports or tests that can never fail, and that is what decides whether a developer can afford to fix the problems. To identify the remaining gaps, we integrated test capabilities from 8 testing methods and conducted an empirical study of their behavior, during which we found two blind spots. First, 12 hours of testing produce thousands of bug reports, far more than the number of genuine defects a mature database is likely to contain. Most reports are false positives caused by dialect or pattern-matching differences, and many of the remaining reports are duplicates. Second, analysis of process-level data reveals that many equivalence-based metamorphic test cases lose their ability to detect defects because of the optimization mechanism. Based on these findings, we summarize and realize these guidelines in GraphWeave, an integrated testing platform for graph databases. This includes a multi-agent system that analyzes the flood of bug reports to produce gating rules for issue filtering and adapter rules for dialect adaptation, and a plan-aware triage routes metamorphic pairs by plan, skipping those that share a plan on the same graph state and therefore cannot detect defects. We apply GraphWeave to NeuG, a recently open-sourced industrial graph database that has not been covered by prior graph database testing work. With modest manual effort, GraphWeave uncovers 19 previously unknown bugs, all of which have since been confirmed.

translation.title: 通过集成与进程级分析揭示图数据库测试中的系统性盲点
translation.abstract: 图数据库正在成为关联数据的基础设施，越来越多的自动化测试技术在成熟的图数据库系统中发现了大量缺陷。每种技术检查正确性的不同方面，暴露不同类别的缺陷。组合这些技术是自然的下一步，但每种技术都以它发现的真实缺陷来评判，而不是以无用报告或永远不会失败的测试来评判，而这决定了开发者是否有能力修复这些问题。为了找出剩余的差距，我们集成了8种测试方法的测试能力，并对它们的行为进行了实证研究，在此过程中发现了两个盲点。第一，12小时的测试会产生数千份缺陷报告，远超成熟数据库可能包含的真实缺陷数量。大多数报告是由方言或模式匹配差异导致的误报，其余报告中很多是重复的。第二，对进程级数据的分析表明，许多基于等价的蜕变测试用例因优化机制而丧失了检测缺陷的能力。基于这些发现，我们总结并实现了这些准则，构建了GraphWeave——一个图数据库集成测试平台。其中包括一个多智能体系统，用于分析海量缺陷报告，生成用于问题过滤的门控规则和用于方言适配的适配器规则；以及一个计划感知的分流机制，按执行计划路由蜕变测试对，跳过那些在同一图状态上共享计划因而无法检测缺陷的测试对。我们将GraphWeave应用于NeuG——一个近期开源、此前未被图数据库测试工作覆盖的工业级图数据库。仅需适度的人工投入，GraphWeave就发现了19个此前未知的缺陷，且全部得到确认。
translation.brief: 针对图数据库测试中误报泛滥和蜕变测试因优化失效两大盲点，集成8种测试方法并通过多智能体报告过滤与计划感知分流构建GraphWeave平台。

papers.title: Automated Video-to-QA Pipeline: End-to-End Question Generation and Verification Using Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The exponential growth of educational and informational video content on platforms like YouTube presents a challenge for efficient knowledge retrieval and assessment. This paper proposes an end-to-end automated pipeline for extracting structured summaries and generating high-fidelity Question-Answer (QA) pairs from video streams. The framework integrates a cascade of state-of-the-art models: audio extraction is handled via FFmpeg, followed by automatic speech recognition (ASR) using Whisper (A library in Python) to generate accurate transcripts. Due to the token constraints of Large Language Models (LLMs), transcripts are segmented and summarized using Facebook's BART. A key innovation of this work is a Self-Verification and Fine-Tuning Loop. We utilize meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8BInstruct to generate candidate QA pairs from transcript chunks, which are then fed back into the model to rigorously assess their relevance and importance. Only verified, high-quality pairs are retained to construct a synthetic dataset. This dataset is subsequently used to fine-tune the Llama model using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), resulting in a specialized model capable of generating domain-aligned assessment questions. This approach demonstrates a scalable method for creating self-improving educational tools without the need for manual data annotation. The proposed model can be downloaded from Kaggle with all the codes from GitHub.

translation.title: 自动化视频转问答流水线：基于大语言模型的端到端问题生成与验证
translation.abstract: YouTube等平台上教育和信息类视频内容的指数级增长，为高效的知识检索与评估带来了挑战。本文提出一个端到端的自动化流水线，用于从视频流中提取结构化摘要并生成高保真的问答（QA）对。该框架集成了多个最先进模型的级联：音频提取通过FFmpeg处理，随后使用Whisper（一个Python库）进行自动语音识别（ASR）以生成准确的转录文本。由于大语言模型（LLM）的token限制，转录文本被分段并使用Facebook的BART进行摘要。本工作的一个关键创新是自我验证与微调循环。我们利用meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct从转录文本片段生成候选QA对，然后将其反馈给模型以严格评估其相关性和重要性。只有经过验证的高质量问答对才会被保留用于构建合成数据集。随后，该数据集被用于通过低秩适应（LoRA）微调Llama模型，得到一个能够生成与领域对齐的评估问题的专用模型。该方法展示了一种无需人工数据标注即可创建自我改进教育工具的可扩展方法。所提出的模型可从Kaggle下载，全部代码可在GitHub获取。
translation.brief: 针对视频内容难以高效转化为评估题的问题，构建从音频转录到LLM生成QA对并自我验证、再用LoRA微调的端到端自动化流水线。

papers.title: RIVER: Evidence-guided multi-agent retrieval for enzyme--reaction discovery
papers.abstract: Enzyme function annotation and the identification of candidate enzymes for a given reaction are essential steps in connecting genomic information to biochemical reaction networks. However, existing methods rely on sequence or structural similarity or on training with known enzyme--reaction pairs, making it difficult to integrate biochemical evidence across large candidate spaces; they also struggle with retrieval tasks involving enzyme families whose members are highly similar. Here, we introduce RIVER (Reaction--enzyme Inference via Evidence-guided Retrieval), a multi-agent framework for bidirectional enzyme--reaction retrieval that identifies potentially catalyzed reactions for a given enzyme and ranks candidate enzymes for a given reaction. RIVER coordinates large language models, specialized biochemical computational tools, and external knowledge resources to assemble evidence at multiple levels, including reaction chemistry, protein sequences and domains, catalytic mechanisms, and database annotations. Dedicated validation modules further examine evidence gaps and potential conflicts and rerank candidates using traceable evidence records. On public benchmarks, RIVER achieves the highest success rates in both enzyme retrieval and enzyme annotation. In family-specific enzyme retrieval, RIVER outperforms the evaluated baselines on the selected datasets and metrics. In Escherichia coli enzyme retrieval tasks constructed from recent literature, RIVER achieves the best retrieval results with closed-source and open-source model configurations, substantially outperforming closed-source general-purpose and biology-specialized multi-agent systems, including Claude Code, Codex, and Phylo Max. These results suggest that evidence-guided multi-agent retrieval can prioritize biochemically supported enzyme--reaction relationships, providing a basis for subsequent experimental validation.

translation.title: RIVER：面向酶-反应发现的证据引导多智能体检索
translation.abstract: 酶功能注释以及为给定反应识别候选酶，是将基因组信息与生化反应网络连接起来的关键步骤。然而，现有方法依赖序列或结构相似性，或依赖已知酶-反应对的训练，难以在大规模候选空间中整合生化证据；在涉及成员高度相似的酶家族的检索任务中也表现不佳。我们提出RIVER（Reaction-enzyme Inference via Evidence-guided Retrieval），一个用于双向酶-反应检索的多智能体框架，可为给定酶识别其可能催化的反应，并为给定反应对候选酶进行排序。RIVER协调大语言模型、专用生化计算工具和外部知识资源，在多个层面收集证据，包括反应化学、蛋白质序列与结构域、催化机制和数据库注释。专门的验证模块进一步检查证据缺口和潜在冲突，并利用可追溯的证据记录对候选进行重排序。在公开基准上，RIVER在酶检索和酶注释两项任务中均取得最高成功率。在家族特异性酶检索中，RIVER在所选数据集和指标上优于被评估的基线。在基于近期文献构建的大肠杆菌酶检索任务中，RIVER在闭源和开源模型配置下均取得最佳检索结果，大幅超越闭源通用型和生物学专用多智能体系统，包括Claude Code、Codex和Phylo Max。这些结果表明，证据引导的多智能体检索能够优先排序有生化证据支持的酶-反应关系，为后续实验验证提供基础。
translation.brief: 针对酶-反应双向检索中难以整合生化证据的问题，提出RIVER多智能体框架，协调LLM、生化工具与知识资源进行多层面证据收集与验证重排序。

papers.title: ReConMem: A Graph-Based Dual Memory System for Repository-Oriented Conversations
papers.abstract: LLM-based code assistants are increasingly used in iterative repository-level development, where effective assistance requires jointly leveraging evolving conversational history and repository context. Existing memory systems, however, are primarily designed for general-purpose conversations and do not sufficiently coordinate conversational information with the structured code entities to which it refers. We propose ReConMem, a graph-based dual memory system for repository-oriented conversations. ReConMem organizes distilled conversational memories and conversation-relevant code entities into interconnected semantic and structural memory graphs, while maintaining their cross-graph associations as interactions evolve. For memory recall, ReConMem combines natural-language and code-aligned retrieval through code-draft-based query grounding, expands retrieved information over intra- and inter-graph relations, and compresses retrieved code according to its structural granularity. We evaluate ReConMem on two repository-oriented conversational benchmarks spanning long-horizon context management and realistic project-grounded multi-turn assistance. On LoCoEval, ReConMem improves Pass@1 over the strongest baseline by 7.917 and 7.292 percentage points on single-hop and multi-hop subsets, respectively, with comparable context compression. On CodeAssistBench, it achieves 27.61% Correct and 44.03% Partially Correct, exceeding Full History by 4.10 and 7.09 percentage points, respectively, while improving interaction quality. These results demonstrate that aligning conversational memory with repository structure improves context management for repository-oriented multi-turn interactions.

translation.title: ReConMem：面向仓库级对话的基于图的双重记忆系统
translation.abstract: 基于LLM的代码助手越来越多地用于迭代式仓库级开发，其中有效的辅助需要同时利用不断演化的对话历史和仓库上下文。然而，现有记忆系统主要面向通用对话设计，未能充分协调对话信息与其所指的结构化代码实体。我们提出ReConMem，一个面向仓库级对话的基于图的双重记忆系统。ReConMem将提炼后的对话记忆和与对话相关的代码实体组织成相互关联的语义记忆图和结构记忆图，并在交互演化过程中维护它们之间的跨图关联。在记忆召回方面，ReConMem通过基于代码草稿的查询锚定结合自然语言检索与代码对齐检索，在图内和跨图关系上扩展检索到的信息，并根据代码的结构粒度对其进行压缩。我们在两个面向仓库级对话的基准上评估ReConMem，涵盖长程上下文管理和真实的基于项目的多轮辅助。在LoCoEval上，ReConMem在单跳和多跳子集上将Pass@1较最强基线分别提升7.917和7.292个百分点，同时保持相当的上下文压缩率。在CodeAssistBench上，它达到27.61%的Correct和44.03%的Partially Correct，较Full History分别超出4.10和7.09个百分点，同时提升了交互质量。这些结果表明，将对话记忆与仓库结构对齐可以改善面向仓库的多轮交互的上下文管理。
translation.brief: 针对现有记忆系统无法协调对话信息与代码实体的问题，提出基于图的语义/结构双重记忆系统ReConMem，通过查询锚定、图关系扩展和结构粒度压缩实现仓库级对话的记忆召回。

papers.title: BiGrounder: Bidirectional Training Unlocks the Potential of GUI Grounding
papers.abstract: Graphical User Interface (GUI) grounding aims to map natural language instructions to precise operational coordinates, serving as a critical task for autonomous agent interaction. Current approaches formalize GUI grounding as predicting action-coordinate pairs from instructions, with end-to-end training supervised solely by final coordinates. Training datasets typically provide only a small number of descriptions per target coordinate, whereas real-world scenarios involve a much larger set of varied descriptions for the same target, which limits robustness to linguistic variation. While recent GUI grounding paradigms have begun employing reinforcement learning to enhance localization accuracy, models with limited exploratory capability before reinforcement yield constrained improvements even with identical training data during the reinforcement phase. To overcome these limitations, we propose a bidirectional reward paradigm that enables model self-reinforcement. During SFT, bidirectional training equips the model to generate action descriptions from target coordinates. During RL, the model samples semantically consistent instruction variations on-policy and grounds each variation back to its target. A cycle-consistency gate couples semantic quality to grounding success, turning the model's own instruction policy into a source of continually refreshed reinforcement trajectories. Our 4B-parameter model achieves competitive accuracy across five grounding benchmarks in our evaluation, indicating the effectiveness of the proposed training paradigm. this https URL

translation.title: BiGrounder：双向训练释放GUI定位的潜力
translation.abstract: 图形用户界面（GUI）定位旨在将自然语言指令映射到精确的操作坐标，是自主智能体交互的关键任务。当前方法将GUI定位形式化为从指令预测动作-坐标对，端到端训练仅由最终坐标监督。训练数据集通常只为每个目标坐标提供少量描述，而真实场景中同一目标存在大量多样的描述，这限制了对语言变化的鲁棒性。尽管近期的GUI定位范式已开始采用强化学习来提升定位精度，但在强化学习之前探索能力有限的模型，即使在强化阶段使用相同训练数据，改进也较为有限。为克服这些局限，我们提出一种使模型自我强化的双向奖励范式。在SFT阶段，双向训练使模型能够从目标坐标生成动作描述。在RL阶段，模型在策略上采样语义一致的指令变体，并将每个变体重新定位回其目标。循环一致性门控将语义质量与定位成功耦合，使模型自身的指令策略成为持续更新的强化轨迹来源。我们的4B参数模型在评估的五个定位基准上取得了有竞争力的准确率，表明所提训练范式的有效性。this https URL
translation.brief: 针对GUI定位训练数据描述单一、强化学习探索受限的问题，提出双向训练范式，让模型从坐标生成指令变体并通过循环一致性门控实现自我强化。

papers.title: Adapt the Object to the Subject: Representative Study Material for Empirical Software Engineering
papers.abstract: External validity is a central concern in empirical software engineering, yet the debate has largely focused on whether study participants are representative. How well the study objects they reason about - code, models, or requirements - are representative of each participant's own work is often overlooked. Practitioners' own artifacts would be ideal, but are often out of reach, so researchers sample from public datasets or construct objects artificially. Whether this lack of subject-object fit affects participants' ability to act on the material remains unknown. We take a first step toward answering this question for requirements. We propose an approach that uses an LLM to generate context-adapted synthetic requirements just-in-time during an online survey from a short, participant-supplied context description, optionally injecting requirements smells as controlled stimuli. To validate the approach, we conducted a controlled experiment with 31 industry practitioners in a 2x2 design that crosses stimulus generation (static vs. synthetic) with quality (clean vs. smelly). Each participant rated the perceived representativeness and assessability of 20 requirements. Using Bayesian data analysis within a statistical causal-inference framework, we find that perceived representativeness has a strong positive effect on assessability. Synthetic requirements are rated as more representative and, primarily due to this gain, more assessable than static ones sourced from public datasets; smell injection leaves both perceptions unchanged. Our results support treating a lack of study-object representativeness as a first-class validity threat and position context-adapted synthetic study objects as a practical addition to the empirical methodology toolbox.

papers.title: Geometry-Evolving Barrier Functions for Safety Evaluation in Dynamic Environments
papers.abstract: Autonomous systems operating in dynamic environments often involve multiple interacting agents, giving rise to high-dimensional safety evaluation problems. Hamilton--Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides rigorous finite-horizon safety guarantees, but solving a global HJ partial differential equation (PDE) over the entire state space leads to prohibitive computational complexity. In this paper, we introduce Geometry-Evolving Barrier Functions (GEBFs), a novel representation for dynamic safety evaluation that propagates local safety geometry of the solution to a terminal-value HJ PDE. By evolving the value, gradient, and curvature information along a Hamiltonian-induced reference trajectory, GEBFs provide a compact representation of the local HJ safety landscape. Under suitable local regularity assumptions, we establish consistency between the GEBF and the value, gradient, and Hessian of the HJ solution along an HJ-optimal characteristic. Building on these theoretical results, we develop an iterative algorithm that couples local geometric propagation with trajectory refinement. We further establish a trajectory-wise one-sided relationship between the GEBF and HJ value function, together with a fixed-point consistency result for the iterative scheme. Experiments on widely adopted agent--obstacle collision-avoidance benchmarks, across low- and high-dimensional systems, demonstrate that GEBFs accurately capture the evolution of dynamic safety boundaries, while achieving substantially lower computational cost than conventional HJ reachability.

papers.title: Decodability Is Not Validity: Evaluating Nuisance Sensitivity in Language Model Concept Probes
papers.abstract: Two concept probes can be equally accurate at predicting a concept from a language model's hidden states while their scores contain different mixtures of the target concept and a correlated nuisance attribute. In four target--nuisance settings (two aspect sentiments in CEBaB; occupation and gender in BiasBios; Amazon review sentiment with negation, and with first-person framing), two LLMs, and a population of concept extractors, we compare decodability with discriminant evidence: the score's dependence on the nuisance at fixed target, and its response to input edits intended to change only the nuisance, filtered by two LLM judges and compared against placebo edits. Under correlated training data, extractors that are statistically equivalent in held-out AUROC differ up to several-fold in nuisance sensitivity in three of the four settings, and decodability is not a reliable proxy for it: their rank correlation changes sign across settings. The effect follows the probe's training data, not the nuisance's natural association with the target: first-person framing, unrelated to sentiment in natural reviews, is absorbed at least as much as negation, which co-occurs with negative sentiment, and decorrelated training removes the systematic effect. Selecting extractors with nuisance-aware development diagnostics, which need nuisance labels but no counterfactuals, lowers counterfactual nuisance sensitivity wherever the default choice is sensitive, at a small accuracy cost. Concept measurements should be validated, not just decoded.

papers.title: Axis-LoRA: Probing and Adapting Embedding Models for Personal-Memory Retrieval
papers.abstract: As LLMs are increasingly asked questions about a user's personal experiences, retrieval must distinguish memories by time, place, person, and event. Current personal-memory pipelines rely on frozen dense embedding models to embed memories for retrieval, but we find that these models do not capture the four axes well. Swapping a memory's date or place barely shifts its embedding, and a trained projection on top of the frozen embedding does not recover the missing signal. The problem lives inside the model, where each axis is encoded by a distinct attention-head pattern. Guided by these findings, we propose Axis-LoRA, a per-axis adapter that places four LoRA branches inside the embedding model and combines them via a per-query gate. Across three standard embedding models evaluated on LongMemEval, ATM-Bench, and LoCoMo, Axis-LoRA improves 4-benchmark mean R@10 by $+1.28$ to $+1.56$~pp while training only a small fraction of the base parameters on a small axis-counterfactual training set. Code is available at this https URL.

papers.title: Generate-then-Rank: Learning Symbolic Goal Interpretation for Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Goal interpretation is to translate a natural language instruction into a formal symbolic goal that a planner can execute. It is critical for embodied agents because any error here propagates to every downstream planning and action step. Doing it well requires both generating suitable candidates and reliably selecting among them. We present a two-stage generate-then-rank approach to Goal Interpretation in the Embodied Agent Interface (EAI). First, supervised fine-tuning adapts a Large Language Model (LLM) to EAI's output convention. Second, Candidate-Output Ranking from Errors (CORE) learns preferences over complete outputs from the model's own generated alternatives. We conducted experiments on the household scenes of the Embodied Agent Interface Benchmark. Multiple open source LLMs including DeepSeek-V3 chat, DeepSeek-Reasoner, and Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-72B were evaluated. The proposed method outperformed the baseline models including LLMs with simple prompting, chain-of-thought, and knowledge graph based approaches.

papers.title: Instantiating the Knowledge Plane
papers.abstract: In 2003, Clark et al. proposed the "Knowledge Plane", a layer of intelligent agents that share rich information about network state in order to collaboratively manage the Internet across administrative boundaries. The technology of the day lacked the two capabilities it demanded most: reasoning and unstructured communication. Thus, automated network management has remained largely confined to single domains, while interdomain problems are still resolved by human operators on the phone. We argue that agentic large language models can finally unlock the potential of the Knowledge Plane, but that doing so will require solving new research problems that arise particularly in this decentralized, multi-agent, coopetitive setting that have received limited attention in the literature thus far.

translation.title: 知识平面的实例化
translation.abstract: 2003年，Clark等人提出了"知识平面"（Knowledge Plane）的概念，即一层共享丰富网络状态信息、以跨管理域协作管理互联网的智能代理。然而当时的技术缺乏它最需要的两种能力：推理和非结构化通信。因此，自动化网络管理在很大程度上仍局限于单一域内，而跨域问题仍由人工运维通过电话解决。我们认为，智能体化大语言模型（agentic LLM）最终能够释放知识平面的潜力，但要做到这一点，需要解决在这种去中心化、多智能体、竞合（coopetitive）环境下产生的新研究问题，而这些问题迄今在文献中受到的关注有限。
translation.brief: 该论文提出用智能体化大语言模型实现Clark等人设想的知识平面，并指出需解决去中心化多智能体竞合环境下的新研究问题。

papers.title: Computation, not weight access: large language models as auditors of clinical prediction networks
papers.abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) have been reported to read, edit and write the weights of small neural networks, raising the prospect of auditing clinical prediction models from their files alone. Public demonstrations, however, mixed reading raw weights with running code. We separated these conditions in internally pre-specified simulation experiments. Tanh networks of 105 to 38,401 weights were trained on simulated cohorts of patients with subarachnoid haemorrhage, each with a planted relationship or none, and one network was trained on labels that under-recorded deaths in a subgroup. GPT-6 Astra and four other GPT models answered single prompts under a default or an explicit system instruction, either with the weights in the prompt and no tools, or with a calculation-only tool that exposed the weights (white box) or only the network's predictions (black box). Without tools, Astra recovered planted relationships in 353-weight networks but became unreliable at 3,457 weights, and under the default instruction it declined 11 of 12 audit and repair tasks as unidentifiable; the explicit instruction removed these refusals. With the tool, it recovered the planted relationship in all 29 runs on networks of up to 38,401 weights, raised no false alarm in 15 runs on null networks, and found the biased subgroup in 6 of 6 runs. Black-box access performed as well as white-box access, and other GPT-6 models read as accurately. A well-designed script matched the comparator models on the audit and the best LLM repair. For auditing these networks, what mattered was computation and elicitation, not access to the weights.

translation.title: 计算而非权重访问：大语言模型作为临床预测网络的审计者
translation.abstract: 已有报道称前沿大语言模型（LLM）能够读取、编辑和编写小型神经网络的权重，这引发了仅凭模型文件审计临床预测模型的前景。然而公开演示将读取原始权重与运行代码混为一谈。我们在内部预先设定的仿真实验中将这些条件分开。在模拟的蛛网膜下腔出血患者队列上训练了105至38,401个权重的Tanh网络，每个网络中植入或不植入某种关系，其中一个网络使用漏记某亚组死亡的标签训练。GPT-6 Astra和其他四个GPT模型在默认或显式系统指令下回答单个提示，要么将权重放入提示且不使用工具，要么使用仅暴露权重（白盒）或仅暴露网络预测（黑盒）的纯计算工具。在没有工具的情况下，Astra能在353权重网络中恢复植入关系，但在3,457权重时变得不可靠，且在默认指令下它以无法识别为由拒绝了12项审计和修复任务中的11项；显式指令消除了这些拒绝。使用工具时，它在所有29次运行中都能恢复最高38,401权重网络中的植入关系，在15次零假设网络运行中未产生误报，并在6次运行中全部发现了有偏亚组。黑盒访问与白盒访问表现相当，其他GPT-6模型的读取精度也相当。一个设计良好的脚本在审计任务上与对比模型持平，并达到最佳LLM修复效果。对于审计这类网络，关键在于计算和引导（elicitation），而非对权重的访问。
translation.brief: 该论文通过仿真实验研究LLM能否仅凭权重文件审计临床预测网络，发现关键在于提供计算工具和恰当引导而非权重访问方式。

papers.title: CANMentor: A Large-Small Model Collaboration Framework for CAN Bus Intrusion Detection
papers.abstract: The Controller Area Network (CAN) bus lacks built-in security mechanisms, making real-time intrusion detection necessary. However, resource and latency constraints limit vehicle-side intrusion detection systems (IDSs) to lightweight models, whose detection performance and generalization can degrade under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. Meanwhile, uploading original CAN messages to the cloud for more powerful model inference risks exposing sensitive vehicle information. We propose CANMentor, a large-small model collaboration framework in which a cloud-side large language model (LLM) teacher supervises vehicle-side lightweight IDS models for CAN bus intrusion detection. Each vehicle first performs local inference, and a privacy-aware generator then produces proxies from the original CAN messages for cloud-side teacher inference to protect data privacy. The vehicle uses the teacher prediction only when the response arrives within a prescribed latency bound and otherwise retains the local prediction; all returned teacher logits are converted into soft targets for periodic knowledge distillation. On non-IID partitions of the ROAD dataset and the HCRL Car-Hacking dataset, knowledge distillation yields maximum relative Macro F1 improvements of 25.01% and 20.79%, respectively. Teacher predictions also improve detection accuracy for CAN messages near the local decision boundary by 38.71-42.00 percentage points.

translation.title: CANMentor：面向CAN总线入侵检测的大小模型协作框架
translation.abstract: 控制器局域网（CAN）总线缺乏内置安全机制，因此实时入侵检测十分必要。然而，资源和时延约束使车端入侵检测系统（IDS）只能使用轻量级模型，其在非独立同分布（non-IID）数据下的检测性能和泛化能力可能下降。同时，将原始CAN报文上传云端以进行更强模型推理存在泄露敏感车辆信息的风险。我们提出CANMentor，一种大小模型协作框架，其中云端大语言模型（LLM）教师监督车端轻量级CAN总线入侵检测模型。每辆车先进行本地推理，随后隐私感知生成器从原始CAN报文生成代理数据供云端教师推理，以保护数据隐私。仅当教师响应在规定时延界限内到达时车辆才采用教师预测，否则保留本地预测；所有返回的教师logits被转换为软目标用于周期性知识蒸馏。在ROAD数据集和HCRL Car-Hacking数据集的non-IID划分上，知识蒸馏分别带来最高25.01%和20.79%的相对Macro F1提升。教师预测还将本地决策边界附近CAN报文的检测准确率提高了38.71-42.00个百分点。
translation.brief: 该论文提出CANMentor框架，用云端LLM教师通过隐私代理数据和知识蒸馏提升车端轻量级CAN总线入侵检测模型在non-IID数据下的性能。

papers.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
papers.abstract: Autoregressive approaches with large language models, such as long chain-of-thought reasoning, have become the default for new AI applications because they reach higher accuracy on a wide range of tasks. In production, however, they give inconsistent answers, require parsing of outputs, and add cost and latency. Decision models address this: given a question and a set of options supplied by the user, they return a probability distribution over the options without autoregressive decoding. We present Drex, a family of four open decision models with 8B (DLM), 9B (v1.5), 35B with 3B active (v2.0), and 27B (Max) parameters. Each request consists of a state (a document, record, or agent context, optionally with images) and questions about it, each asking for a choice among options, a yes/no judgment, or a score on an ordered scale. Training combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning from adjusted feedback (RLAF), plus vision tuning for Max. Ablations show that RLAF improves accuracy and that consistency losses improve robustness to option order. On Decision Index 0.4.1, Max sets a new state of the art among the decision models we compare (67.52 on the public suite vs. 60.70 for Jev 1.14.0). On Decision Bench v4, it is statistically tied with d3-turbo and GPT-6 Sol and trails Claude Opus 5.5 by 1.6 points, and it has the highest accuracy among decision models on DecideBench. Max answers a typical request in 183 ms, against about 2.0 s for GPT-6 Sol and 3.5 s for Claude Opus 5.5, and its outputs are stable under option reordering. All four models are open source: this https URL

translation.title: 迈向基础决策模型：Drex
translation.abstract: 基于大语言模型的自回归方法（如长思维链推理）因在广泛任务上达到更高准确率，已成为新AI应用的默认选择。但在生产环境中，它们给出不一致的答案、需要解析输出，并增加成本和时延。决策模型解决了这一问题：给定问题和用户提供的选项集，它们无需自回归解码即可返回选项上的概率分布。我们提出Drex，一个包含四个开源决策模型的系列，参数量分别为8B（DLM）、9B（v1.5）、35B激活3B（v2.0）和27B（Max）。每个请求包含一个状态（文档、记录或智能体上下文，可选图像）和关于它的问题，每类问题要求在选项中选择、做出是/否判断或在有序量表上打分。训练结合监督微调与调整反馈的强化学习（RLAF），Max还进行了视觉调优。消融实验表明RLAF提升准确率，一致性损失提升对选项顺序的鲁棒性。在Decision Index 0.4.1上，Max在我们比较的决策模型中创造了新的最先进水平（公开套件67.52分，对比Jev 1.14.0的60.70分）。在Decision Bench v4上，它与d3-turbo和GPT-6 Sol统计上持平，落后Claude Opus 5.5 1.6分，并在DecideBench上拥有决策模型中最高的准确率。Max回答典型请求仅需183毫秒，而GPT-6 Sol约需2.0秒，Claude Opus 5.5约需3.5秒，且其输出在选项重排下保持稳定。全部四个模型均已开源：this https URL
translation.brief: 该论文提出开源决策模型系列Drex，通过监督微调加RLAF强化学习训练，无需自回归解码即可直接输出选项概率分布。

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research
papers.abstract: Deep research agents answer complex questions through repeated search. They rely on a harness that runs their tool calls and returns evidence to their context. This creates a trade-off: Search works best over long passages, which give enough context for reliable semantic matching. But the returned evidence should be short, because every observation stays in the agent's context for the rest of the trajectory. We introduce CORE, a training-free harness that combines coarse-to-fine search with context management. CORE retrieves passages with a dense retriever. It then reuses the token-level similarities from a late-interaction reranker to return only the most relevant snippet from each passage. Context management lets the agent expand the context around sources it has already retrieved and suppresses repeated snippets. In controlled closed-search comparisons with the Tongyi DeepResearch and OpenResearcher harnesses, CORE achieves state-of-the-art answer accuracy and evidence recall across three agent models and three benchmarks (BrowseComp-Plus, BrowseComp-Wikipedia and BrowseComp-Plus-CM), on corpora containing up to 553M documents.

translation.title: CORE：面向深度研究的粗到细搜索与上下文管理
translation.abstract: 深度研究智能体通过反复搜索回答复杂问题。它们依赖一个运行工具调用并将证据返回到其上下文的框架（harness）。这带来一个权衡：搜索在长段落上效果最佳，因为长段落为可靠的语义匹配提供足够上下文；但返回的证据应当简短，因为每条观察都会在后续轨迹中一直留在智能体的上下文中。我们提出CORE，一个无需训练的框架，将粗到细搜索与上下文管理相结合。CORE先用稠密检索器检索段落，然后复用late-interaction重排器的token级相似度，仅返回每个段落中最相关的片段。上下文管理允许智能体扩展已检索来源周围的上下文，并抑制重复片段。在与Tongyi DeepResearch和OpenResearcher框架的受控封闭搜索对比中，CORE在三个智能体模型和三个基准（BrowseComp-Plus、BrowseComp-Wikipedia和BrowseComp-Plus-CM）上、在多达5.53亿文档的语料库上，取得了最先进的答案准确率和证据召回率。
translation.brief: 该论文提出无需训练的CORE框架，通过粗到细搜索与上下文管理解决深度研究智能体中长上下文搜索与短证据返回之间的权衡。

papers.title: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Latent Reasoning for Efficient LLM-Based Recommendation
papers.abstract: LLM-based recommender systems increasingly generate chain-of-thought (CoT) text before each item prediction to activate the LLM's reasoning capacity, costing tens to hundreds of extra tokens per recommendation at inference. We ask whether inference-time reasoning artifacts (textual or latent) can be replaced by training-time supervision alone, without loss of accuracy. We propose LatentRec, a framework for LLM-based generative recommendation that replaces inference-time reasoning artifacts with training-time per-step head supervision. LatentRec has three components. A 2.5M-parameter Continuous Thought Module iterates K latent reasoning steps over the LLM's hidden state during training. Soft Token Selection bridges the ~14x norm gap between hidden states and input embeddings. A Per-step Reasoning Loss (PRL) supervises every intermediate state through the LLM's prediction head against the first token of the target Semantic ID. The trained LLM retains this accuracy without the module at inference, so the module can be discarded at deployment. On three Amazon benchmarks, LatentRec improves HR@10 by 4.0-5.0% (relative) over a CoT-distilled baseline at 18.3x lower latency (batch=1). Per-step training supervision consistently improves accuracy across three datasets, paid once at training rather than at every recommendation.

papers.title: Compositional Loop Invariant Inference for Multiphase Programs via Structured Neurosymbolic Reasoning
papers.abstract: Loop invariants are essential for deductive program verification, yet automatically inferring them for {multiphase programs}, whose loops contain conditional branches that induce multiple execution phases with distinct behaviors, remains an open problem. Existing LLM-based methods either reason about loops as a whole or use explicit branch information to generate atomic assertions jointly across branches, without maintaining complete candidate sub-invariants for independent generation and targeted repair. We present CLOVER, a structured neurosymbolic reasoning framework for multiphase invariant inference built on two interlinked mechanisms. First, compositional inference: CLOVER statically decomposes a loop into symbolic {loop branch sequences}, conjunctions of the loop guard and branch conditions that characterize distinct execution scenarios, and guides the LLM to generate candidate sub-invariants for each one independently, so that each LLM query focuses on a single execution scenario rather than the entire loop. Second, counterexample-guided localized refinement: when SMT verification rejects a composed disjunctive invariant, CLOVER traces the counterexample back through the branch structure to identify which specific loop branch sequence caused the failure and repairs only that sub-invariant, preserving all correct components. Both mechanisms are unified by a shared symbolic structure derived from the loop's branch semantics, which guides what the LLM generates, how candidates are composed, and where refinement is directed. We evaluate CLOVER on 316 linear arithmetic, 50 nonlinear arithmetic, and 54 multiphase benchmarks. CLOVER solves 35 of 54 multiphase benchmarks, outperforming the best LLM-based baseline (29) by 20.7\% and the best traditional method (22) by 59.1\%. On linear/nonlinear benchmarks, CLOVER remains competitive, solving 355 of 366 programs overall.

papers.title: A Low Similarity Score Does Not Show Independence after Source-Conditioned Repository Rewriting
papers.abstract: Maintainers sometimes cite a low token-similarity score as evidence that an LLM-assisted rewrite of a copyleft project is independent of the original. We test what such a score can support under \emph{source-conditioned} rewriting: a coding agent keeps the original in its working copy, rewrites the repository, and iterates until a fixed behavioural harness passes, with no human edit to the code. On 69 rewrites of six copyleft Python projects we find that: \ding{182}~Agent-only rewriting is inexpensive and often yields low scores. Every controlled rewrite passes the harness after repair, usually within half an hour for the initial rewrite. Under a ground-up rearchitecture prompt, most rewrites fall below 25\% JPlag similarity and still pass the harness. \ding{183}~A single low score is an unreliable witness. Identical project--agent--prompt configurations produce wide spreads in similarity; run-to-run variation dominates project and agent effects, and in more than a third of configurations the three repeats straddle the threshold. Rewrites retain more of the original's imports and fingerprint facts than unrelated projects do, yet hand-written independent implementations of the same task often retain as much, and neither signal separates the two groups better than chance. Thus a low score on one rewrite is weak evidence of independence: another run of the same agent may score high. Claims based on similarity should report repeated generations, and candidate provenance signals should be checked against same task independent implementations, not only against unrelated projects.

papers.title: Persistent Retrieval for Conversational Agents: A Study of Retrieval Efficiency
papers.abstract: Conversational agents can retrieve information directly or delegate retrieval to a subagent. This design choice affects how retrieval history is maintained, what context each model call receives, and what information must be re-retrieved in follow-up questions. We compare three designs: skill-based retrieval in the main agent, a non-persistent retrieval subagent that generates a findings response, and our persistent retrieval subagent, which maintains retrieval history across turns and returns retrieved evidence directly to the main agent. Our approach also allows the main agent to request corrections from the same subagent. We evaluate the three designs on enterprise questions posed independently, within shared conversations, and as dependent follow-ups. Across five multi-turn settings, our approach uses 43.3% fewer recorded agent-model tokens and incurs 45.0% lower estimated API cost than skill-based retrieval, while reducing average response time by 9.1%. Compared with non-persistent retrieval, it reduces response time by 15.6 seconds per question, while using 65.1% more tokens and incurring 29.1% higher estimated API cost. Our approach shifts the retrieval subagent from producing synthesized responses to maintaining retrieval state and supplying evidence that the main agent can directly evaluate and use for answer generation.

papers.title: ZeroRAG: Adaptive Semantic Peer Routing for Decentralized Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a standard approach to enhance the reliability of large language model (LLM) outputs by retrieving documents relevant to a query and supplying them in the LLM prompt. Today's RAG systems collect, index, and serve these documents from centralized stores. In practice, however, documents are owned by organizations, devices, and individuals who cannot or will not surrender custody of them to a central party, e.g., because of privacy, copyright or regulatory compliance. Existing modern decentralized retrieval techniques either reintroduce a coordinating authority, or rely on a global data structure that requires continuous network-wide coordination (e.g., DHTs). We present ZeroRAG, a decentralized routing layer for document retrieval in RAG that performs semantic query routing across an overlay of peers with- out global data structures or centralized orchestration. Documents remain with the peers that own them, and each peer keeps only lightweight local state: a bounded set of neighbor advertisements and a cache of recently routed queries. Using these, ZeroRAG steers each query through a best-first walk that progressively rewires the overlay toward semantically relevant neighbors, so recall improves over time as the network self-organizes. We evaluate ZeroRAG using three real-world workloads and two decentralized baselines. We find that ZeroRAG outperforms baselines in terms of recall and required network messages, approaches the recall and LLM answer accuracy of a centralized document store, self-heals after catastrophic peer failures, and scales to 100 000 peers.

papers.title: AttnSR: Attention Step Reward for Long-Horizon Agentic RL
papers.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents make multi-step decisions, yet outcome-reward-only reinforcement learning provides little direct supervision for individual steps. We introduce AttnSR, a step-level reward augmentation method that derives reward allocations from policy attention extracted during training replay, without a separately trained reward model or additional rollouts. AttnSR traces backward through the policy model attention graph to estimate the relevance of earlier steps to the final response. The terminal step, measured relative to a running baseline, determines whether these rewards reinforce or penalize the selected steps. In a controlled Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct study, AttnSR consistently outperforms the PPO baseline across all evaluated checkpoints on ALFWorld, raising final held-out success from 91.2% to 97.1%. The ablation experiment shows that the benefit depends on how intermediate rewards are assigned, rather than simple accumulation of step rewards over time. AttnSR also improves ScienceWorld at every checkpoint while cutting environment interactions by 29.9%. These results support policy attention as a practical prior for step-level reward allocation in long-horizon agentic RL. Code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: The Blindfolded Controller: Decision Model-Guided Training for Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) provides a framework for continuous improvement through interaction with an environment. However, RL agents struggle against tasks that offer exploration challenges and sparse rewards, because learning efficient policies from scratch is slow and sample-inefficient. In contrast, decision models (DMs), given a description of the environment and task, can perform well in sparse-reward tasks, but, as they do not learn from reward, they are not able to improve towards the optimal solution. In this paper, we present Decision Model-Guided Training (DMGT), a technique that uses a DM with a description of the environment and task to initialise an RL policy, combining the DM's ability to act without training with RL's ability to improve from reward. Instead of exploring from scratch, the agent reaches the goal and receives reward from its first episodes, and RL then improves its policy beyond what the DM achieves. We demonstrate through experiments on seven tasks that our approach outperforms RL in all seven and DM in five. In addition, we provide comprehensive guidelines, derived from ablation studies, for describing an environment and task to a DM.

papers.title: tok: a textual concrete syntax of BPMN and DMN for humans and AI agents
papers.abstract: tok is a plain-text notation for Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) 2.0.2 process models and Decision Model and Notation (DMN) 1.5 decisions. One engine checks a tok document against both standards, compiles the document to XML with an automatic diagram, and serves language-model applications through the Model Context Protocol. The paper classifies the notation as an alternative concrete syntax of the BPMN and DMN metamodels and reports one study. A tok model takes 2.2 times fewer tokens than the smallest BPMN XML of 893 files exported by 37 tools and 7.7 times fewer than the files as exported. The checker signals 98.2% of 1,411 injected faults, against 85.8% for the XML Schema with bpmnlint. Four language models new to tok write valid tok from a one-page reference for 85.7 to 100% of 87 process descriptions from two datasets and valid BPMN XML for every description, and the strongest model writes tok with 25% and 19% fewer tokens than BPMN XML. As agents with a lean skill and one checker tool, the models write valid tok for 97.6 to 100% of the descriptions, the strongest model spends 21% and 14% fewer tokens on tok than on BPMN XML, and a skill which sends the model to read the reference through a tool costs 1.7 to 2.8 times the tokens of the lean skill. Of 47 event logs simulated from public models, 44 fit their source models, and tok imports every model discovered from the logs.

papers.title: ChemE-as-Code: An Open-Source Platform for Agentic AI in Chemical Engineering
papers.abstract: ChemE-as-Code provides an open-source environment in which AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) can carry out chemical engineering work and engineers can check it. Its calculation tools range from catalysis through process simulation to plant layout, HAZOP and life cycle assessment, and skills tell a general-purpose agent how to use them. Engineering files are linked, machine-readable and versioned in Git; calculations run outside the LLM, each value records its origin, and automated checks report inconsistencies and out-of-date results by file and line. In an illustrative ammonia case, agents developed a written task into a preliminary basic-engineering package (simulation files, P&IDs, layout, HAZOP, datasheets, relief) for USD 224 of API cost in the design sessions. Planted faults and engineering changes show that the checks find what their rules cover and miss the rest, so they guide human review rather than replace it. No independent engineer has reviewed the design.

papers.title: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, evaluating the correctness of their responses is crucial for reliable use. However, such evaluation is challenging because reference answers are rarely available in practice. Existing reference-free methods mainly rely on output signals, which may assign high scores to incorrect responses and thus do not necessarily reflect correctness. This motivates exploring the model's internal computation for complementary correctness signals. Recent studies exploit internal states, but they mainly analyze hidden-state trajectories across layers, which record only the combined updates of attention and feed-forward networks (FFNs) and overlook how these components interact. We therefore propose Circe, a training-free self-evaluation method that assesses a response using both internal and external signals, without reference answers or repeated sampling. For internal signals, we first introduce component interaction consistency (CIC), which measures the directional alignment between attention updates in earlier layers and attention-induced FFN output changes in later layers. We further incorporate representation geometry (RG) to characterize normalized displacement and angular changes along layerwise hidden-state trajectories. For the external signal, we convert the mean negative log-likelihood of generated tokens into a bounded likelihood confidence (LC) score. Finally, we fuse CIC, RG, and LC into a unified correctness score. Experiments on five LLMs and six benchmarks across four domains show that our method distinguishes correct from incorrect responses more effectively than existing baselines, and generalizes to multilingual, multimodal, and open-world settings.
