papers.title: TCSExam: Evaluating Frontier LLMs on the Full Range of TCS Research
papers.abstract: Can large language models (LLMs) advance theoretical computer science and resolve its long-standing open conjectures? To study progress toward this goal, we introduce TCSExam, a unified framework and benchmark covering the full range of TCS research. It evaluates theorem proving, solver engineering, and constructions alongside direct attempts to resolve open conjectures, capturing both concrete research accomplishments and progress toward long-standing research goals. TCSExam-Full contains 100 expert-reviewed tasks, with submissions checked by the Lean kernel or an executable task checker. TCSExam-Lite selects 20 tasks, five per track, reducing the number of task attempts by 80% at the same per-attempt budget. We evaluate eight agents on Full and nine on Lite. The TCSExam Index combines all four tracks: GPT-6 Astra leads Full (71.9), and Opus 5.5 leads Lite (72.3). Full and Lite rankings are strongly aligned across eight shared agents (Spearman's $\rho=0.93$), supporting Lite as a compact, discriminative benchmark. The evaluations yield improved solver outputs and mathematical constructions, together with independently verified special cases and bounds from open-conjecture attempts. TCSExam provides an extensible framework with task sources, Docker build recipes, and evaluation tools for reproducible use.

translation.title: TCSExam：评估前沿LLM在理论计算机科学研究全范围上的能力
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）能否推动理论计算机科学（TCS）的发展并解决其长期悬而未决的猜想？为研究这一目标的进展，我们提出TCSExam，一个覆盖TCS研究全范围的统一框架与基准。它评估定理证明、求解器工程与构造，以及对开放猜想的直接求解尝试，同时捕捉具体研究成果和朝长期研究目标的进展。TCSExam-Full包含100个经专家评审的任务，提交结果由Lean内核或可执行任务检查器验证。TCSExam-Lite选取20个任务（每个赛道5个），在相同单次尝试预算下将任务尝试次数减少80%。我们在Full上评估了八个agent，在Lite上评估了九个。TCSExam指数综合四个赛道：GPT-6 Astra在Full上领先（71.9），Opus 5.5在Lite上领先（72.3）。在八个共享agent上，Full与Lite的排名高度一致（Spearman's ρ=0.93），支持Lite作为紧凑且有区分度的基准。评估产出了改进的求解器输出和数学构造，以及经独立验证的开放猜想尝试的特殊情形与界。TCSExam提供可扩展框架，包含任务来源、Docker构建配方和评估工具，以支持可复现使用。
translation.brief: 为评估LLM在理论计算机科学研究全范围（定理证明、求解器工程、构造及开放猜想求解）上的能力，构建了经专家评审、可自动验证的统一基准TCSExam及其精简版Lite。

papers.title: QRAE: Query-Relevant Attention Entropy for Context Compression in DeepSearch Agents
papers.abstract: DeepSearch LLM agents repeatedly search and carry retrieved sources into subsequent reasoning steps. This expanding context increases token consumption and latency, although many results do not contribute to later reasoning. We propose Query-Relevant Attention Entropy (QRAE), an online context compression method that uses sparse evidence-assessment heads to decide which intact retrieved chunks should persist across reasoning steps. It scores bounded candidate batches through paired prefills: a query-free control suppresses shared attention responses, while normalized entropy measures the breadth of the positive response within each chunk. High-scoring chunks enter a persistent evidence whitelist and are included in the reasoning context. Uncertain chunks remain outside the reasoning context but are retained in a candidate cache, where they can be retrieved for later reevaluation. QRAE requires neither an additional generative compression pass nor modification of the attention operator. Across multiple DeepSearch benchmarks and reasoning models, QRAE improves task success by an average of 2.35 percentage points and reduces end-to-end latency and reported token usage by an average of 30% and 45%, respectively. These benefits generalize to a model with nearly 100B parameters.

translation.title: QRAE：面向DeepSearch agent上下文压缩的查询相关注意力熵
translation.abstract: DeepSearch LLM agent反复搜索并将检索到的来源带入后续推理步骤。这种不断扩展的上下文增加了token消耗和延迟，尽管许多结果对后续推理并无贡献。我们提出查询相关注意力熵（QRAE），一种在线上下文压缩方法，使用稀疏的证据评估头决定哪些完整的检索块应在推理步骤间保留。它通过成对prefill对有界的候选批次打分：无查询的对照组抑制共享注意力响应，而归一化熵衡量每个块内正向响应的广度。高分块进入持久证据白名单并被纳入推理上下文。不确定的块留在推理上下文之外，但保留在候选缓存中，可在后续重新评估时被检索。QRAE既不需要额外的生成式压缩过程，也不需要修改注意力算子。在多个DeepSearch基准和推理模型上，QRAE平均提升任务成功率2.35个百分点，端到端延迟和报告的token使用量分别平均降低30%和45%。这些收益可推广到近1000亿参数的模型。
translation.brief: 针对DeepSearch agent上下文膨胀导致的token消耗与延迟问题，提出利用成对prefill计算查询相关注意力熵来在线筛选保留哪些检索块的上下文压缩方法QRAE。

papers.title: How Far Can Lightweight LLMs Go in Intent-to-SLO Translation?
papers.abstract: Intent-based networking (IBN) promises QoS provisioning in which the network derives the configuration from operator-stated goals. Its first step, translating a natural-language intent into enforceable service-level objectives (SLOs) grounded in a live snapshot of the network state, increasingly relies on large language models (LLMs). These large models add cost and energy to the management loop and typically require multi-GPU, cloud-hosted infrastructure. Can lightweight open LLMs take over this step dependably? We answer this question with a five-dimensional evaluation of ten LLMs with <10B parameters from five families, under four prompting setups, on 716 placement intents. We evaluate translation performance, intent validation, hallucination, energy impact, and robustness to diverse phrasing. The best configurations translate intents with a strict F1 of 0.943 and reject up to 191 of 195 invalid intents. With few-shot reasoning, the strongest models hallucinate unsupported QoS requirements in only about one response in a hundred, whereas the zero-shot setup struggles. A translated intent costs 0.044-0.148 Wh of GPU energy without reasoning, and added energy cost for reasoning pays off for the weaker models. Furthermore, we show that realistic rephrasing lowers the rejection of invalid intents in 15 of 16 configurations for the best-performing models, leaving robust intent validation as a key open challenge for reliable IBN. Our code and data are available: this https URL.

translation.title: 轻量级LLM在意图到SLO翻译中能走多远？
translation.abstract: 基于意图的网络（IBN）承诺实现QoS供给，即网络从运营商声明的目标推导配置。其第一步是将自然语言意图翻译为基于网络实时状态快照的可执行服务级目标（SLO），这一步日益依赖大语言模型（LLM）。这些大模型给管理环路增加了成本和能耗，且通常需要多GPU云端基础设施。轻量级开源LLM能否可靠地接管这一步？我们通过对来自五个家族的十个参数量小于10B的LLM，在四种提示设置下、针对716个放置意图进行五维评估来回答这一问题。我们评估翻译性能、意图校验、幻觉、能耗影响以及对多样表述的鲁棒性。最佳配置以0.943的严格F1翻译意图，并在195个无效意图中拒绝多达191个。采用少样本推理时，最强模型仅在约百分之一的响应中幻觉出不支持的QoS要求，而零样本设置表现挣扎。翻译一个意图在不使用推理时消耗0.044-0.148 Wh的GPU能量，而推理带来的额外能耗对较弱模型是值得的。此外，我们表明现实的重述会降低最佳模型在16个配置中15个对无效意图的拒绝率，使鲁棒的意图校验成为可靠IBN的关键开放挑战。我们的代码和数据见：this https URL。
translation.brief: 通过五维评估考察参数量小于10B的轻量级开源LLM能否可靠地将自然语言网络意图翻译为可执行的SLO，并分析其幻觉、能耗与鲁棒性。

papers.title: Compression Through a Context Lens: Evaluating Adaptation, Quantization, and Distillation in Arabic Legal LLMs
papers.abstract: Model compression can facilitate the deployment of large language models in resource-constrained legal settings, but its effects on domain-specific performance may depend on the evaluation protocol. We investigate this issue using ArabLegalEval, a Saudi Arabic legal benchmark, under both with-context and no-context evaluation. The former provides supporting legal passages, while the latter assesses performance without external context. Removing the context produces accuracy gaps of up to 27 percentage points for the base model. We examine three stages: domain adaptation, quantization, and knowledge distillation across FANAR-9B, JAIS-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B. Four-bit quantization reduces model memory by 64-71%, with changes in no-context MCQ accuracy ranging from -3.2 to +1.6 percentage points. Distillation produces more variable results, with accuracy generally declining as student size decreases. A Qwen2.5-7B student distilled from FANAR achieves 76.6% no-context accuracy, compared with 77.2% for its teacher. Our findings suggest that no-context evaluation provides a useful complement to context-supported testing when assessing the effects of adaptation and compression on Arabic legal language models.

translation.title: 通过上下文视角看压缩：评估阿拉伯语法律LLM中的适配、量化与蒸馏
translation.abstract: 模型压缩可以促进大语言模型在资源受限法律场景中的部署，但其对领域特定性能的影响可能取决于评估协议。我们使用沙特阿拉伯语法律基准ArabLegalEval，在带上下文和无上下文两种评估下研究这一问题。前者提供支持性法律段落，后者在无外部上下文的情况下评估性能。移除上下文使基础模型的准确率差距高达27个百分点。我们考察三个阶段：FANAR-9B、JAIS-8B和Qwen2.5-7B上的领域适配、量化和知识蒸馏。4比特量化将模型内存减少64-71%，无上下文MCQ准确率变化范围为-3.2到+1.6个百分点。蒸馏结果变化更大，准确率通常随学生模型规模减小而下降。由FANAR蒸馏得到的Qwen2.5-7B学生模型达到76.6%的无上下文准确率，而其教师为77.2%。我们的发现表明，在评估适配和压缩对阿拉伯语法律语言模型的影响时，无上下文评估为带上下文测试提供了有用的补充。
translation.brief: 研究领域适配、量化和蒸馏三种压缩手段对阿拉伯语法律LLM性能的影响，并发现无上下文评估是揭示压缩效果的重要补充协议。

papers.title: SEER: A Scalable Event-Driven Runtime for Parallel Execution of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Environments
papers.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is increasingly used in systems where many entities interact in a shared environment. In these workloads, policy inference can be batched on GPUs, but the CPU-side environment path still updates entity states, resolves local interactions, and builds observations inside each $\mathrm{this http URL}$. This path can dominate latency in interaction-intensive workloads after policy batching. Existing vectorized environment interfaces and general event-driven runtimes do not directly address the fine-grained cross-entity work inside one bounded MARL step while preserving the step-level semantics expected by learning systems. We present SEER (Scalable Event-Driven Environment Runtime), a runtime for MARL environment execution under an explicit event-locality contract. SEER models each environment step as a bounded stream of timestamped events. If direct state updates are entity-local and cross-entity effects are represented as ordered future events, SEER can run independent events in parallel while preserving serial-equivalent boundary outputs. To make this contract practical, SEER uses a CAS-based dual-layer event queue: local event queues preserve per-entity causal order, while a parallel executive list exposes ready work to global worker threads. SEER further uses STPA, a preflight-guided thread-pool selection mechanism that combines short runtime traces with static workload and hardware features. We evaluate SEER on two parameterized MARL workloads: compute-intensive UAV swarm control (Aircraft) and communication-intensive wireless management (PCS). On Aircraft, SEER reduces inference latency by 16.2\% over the baseline. On PCS, SEER reduces environment-execution latency by 46.9\%, 19.5\%, and 64.9\% over ROSS-T, NBSE, and ROOT-Sim, respectively.

translation.title: SEER：面向多智能体强化学习环境并行执行的可扩展事件驱动运行时
translation.abstract: 多智能体强化学习（MARL）日益用于大量实体在共享环境中交互的系统。在这类工作负载中，策略推理可以在GPU上批处理，但CPU侧的环境路径仍需在每个this http URL内更新实体状态、解决局部交互并构建观测。在策略批处理之后，这条路径可能在交互密集型工作负载中主导延迟。现有的向量化环境接口和通用事件驱动运行时并未直接解决单个有界MARL步骤内的细粒度跨实体工作，同时保持学习系统所期望的步骤级语义。我们提出SEER（Scalable Event-Driven Environment Runtime），一个在显式事件局部性契约下执行MARL环境的运行时。SEER将每个环境步骤建模为带时间戳事件的有界流。如果直接状态更新是实体局部的，且跨实体效应被表示为有序的未来事件，SEER可以并行运行独立事件，同时保持串行等价的边界输出。为使该契约实用，SEER使用基于CAS的双层事件队列：局部事件队列保持每实体的因果顺序，而并行执行列表将就绪工作暴露给全局工作线程。SEER进一步使用STPA，一种结合短运行时轨迹与静态工作负载和硬件特征的预检引导线程池选择机制。我们在两个参数化的MARL工作负载上评估SEER：计算密集的无人机集群控制（Aircraft）和通信密集的无线管理（PCS）。在Aircraft上，SEER比基线降低推理延迟16.2%。在PCS上，SEER相对ROSS-T、NBSE和ROOT-Sim分别降低环境执行延迟46.9%、19.5%和64.9%。
translation.brief: 针对MARL环境中CPU侧细粒度跨实体更新主导延迟的问题，提出基于事件局部性契约和CAS双层事件队列的并行事件驱动运行时SEER。

papers.title: Automatic keyphrase extraction and annotation: modern theoretical approaches and practical solutions for text and speech
papers.abstract: The exponential growth of textual and audiovisual information has made the task of automatic keyphrase extraction (KE) increasingly significant. This article provides a comprehensive analysis of contemporary theoretical approaches and practical solutions for KE across both text and speech modalities. The primary contribution of this work is its systematic synthesis of these often-disparate research strands into a unified analytical framework, highlighting the evolution of the field from statistical methods towards large language models (LLMs) and end-to-end speech processing. We examine the stages of KE, the characteristics of keyphrases in written and spoken language, and terminological nuances. Various methods for automatic KE are discussed and analyzed in detail: statistical, hybrid, machine learning-based, and structural. The review dedicates substantial attention to emerging paradigms, including keyphrase generation using LLMs, and provides a detailed overview of methodologies and challenges in automatic corpus annotation. Furthermore, we specifically analyze current directions and inherent difficulties in KE for spoken language, comparing transcript based and end-to-end acoustic approaches. This synthesis leads us to conclude that the field is moving towards a more integrated, context-aware paradigm. Future progress will depend on addressing key challenges such as data scarcity for low-resource languages, effective multimodal fusion, and the nuanced evaluation of generative KE systems.

translation.title: 自动关键词抽取与标注：面向文本和语音的现代理论方法与实践方案
translation.abstract: 文本和视听信息的指数级增长使得自动关键词抽取（KE）任务日益重要。本文对文本和语音两种模态下KE的当代理论方法与实践方案进行了全面分析。本文的主要贡献是将这些往往彼此割裂的研究脉络系统地综合为一个统一的分析框架，展示了该领域从统计方法向大语言模型（LLM）和端到端语音处理的演进。我们考察了KE的各个阶段、书面语和口语中关键词的特征以及术语上的细微差别。文中详细讨论和分析了多种自动KE方法：统计方法、混合方法、基于机器学习的方法和结构化方法。本综述重点关注新兴范式，包括使用LLM进行关键词生成，并详细概述了自动语料库标注的方法与挑战。此外，我们专门分析了口语KE的当前方向与固有困难，比较了基于转写文本的方法和端到端声学方法。这一综合分析使我们得出结论：该领域正朝着更加融合、上下文感知的范式发展。未来的进展将取决于解决低资源语言数据稀缺、有效的多模态融合以及生成式KE系统的细致评估等关键挑战。
translation.brief: 该综述系统梳理了文本与语音模态下自动关键词抽取的理论方法与实践方案，将其统一到从统计方法到LLM和端到端语音处理的演进框架中。

papers.title: KeHoSu: Keyed Homoglyph Substitution for Authenticated Text Provenance over Copy-Paste Channels
papers.abstract: Nowadays, large language models produce text at scale, and much of it is redistributed across platforms. A moderator who finds a suspicious comment, post or article may want to know which platform generated it and for which account. In this paper we study attribution over the channel through which such text actually travels, copy-paste, which discards document metadata but keeps Unicode code points. We present KeHoSu, which turns the confusable characters of homoglyph attacks into a keyed attribution channel: the variant chosen for each carrier letter encodes one bit of an identifier made of a platform field, a user field and a truncated authentication tag. Moreover, given that reshared text is often quoted in fragments, and the placement therefore keeps no positional state, we show that KeHoSu is invariant to sentence reordering up to a constant boundary layer and depends on a partial quotation only through the retained length. We characterize the code-point channel by its capacity, removability and detectability, and provide an achievable region that relates the three. We evaluate KeHoSu over a wide range of use cases and show that the mark survived copy-paste across 18 common platforms, attributing the majority of all excerpts to the correct account at 178 letters (about two sentences) on LLM-generated stories and 167 letters (about one sentence) on standard English prose.

translation.title: KeHoSu：基于键控同形字替换的复制粘贴通道认证文本溯源
translation.abstract: 如今，大语言模型大规模生成文本，其中大量文本在各平台间被转发。当审核者发现可疑的评论、帖子或文章时，可能想知道它由哪个平台生成、属于哪个账号。本文研究此类文本实际传播的通道——复制粘贴——上的归因问题，该通道会丢弃文档元数据但保留Unicode码点。我们提出KeHoSu，将同形字攻击中的易混淆字符转化为键控归因通道：为每个载体字母选择的变体编码标识符的一个比特，该标识符由平台字段、用户字段和截断的认证标签组成。此外，考虑到被转发的文本常以片段形式被引用，其位置信息因此无法保持，我们证明KeHoSu在句子重排下（除一个常数边界层外）保持不变，且对部分引用的依赖仅体现在保留的长度上。我们用容量、可移除性和可检测性刻画码点通道，并给出关联三者的可达区域。我们在广泛的用例上评估KeHoSu，结果表明该标记在18个常见平台的复制粘贴中得以保留，在LLM生成的故事上以178个字母（约两句话）、在标准英文散文上以167个字母（约一句话）将大多数摘录正确归因到对应账号。
translation.brief: 该论文提出KeHoSu，利用同形字变体在复制粘贴通道中嵌入键控标识符，实现跨平台文本溯源归因。

papers.title: When Imperfect Automated Fact-Checking Backfires: Social Learning in the Presence of Misinformation
papers.abstract: Automated fact-checking tools, cheap and fast but imperfect, are increasingly available on social platforms. We study when such tools can backfire in a sequential social learning model of misinformation. Agents observe an article's reliability and their predecessors' actions, which indicate whether they liked or disliked the article. They may also pay to fact-check it. We examine how welfare, defined as the probability of a correct cascade, changes when a free, error-prone automated tool supplements costly but perfectly accurate manual fact-checking. Two opposing effects arise. Broader use of fact-checking helps agents escape wrong cascades. At the same time, errors from the automated tool can mislead agents who would otherwise have verified the article perfectly, reducing the likelihood of correct cascades. We prove that adding the tool strictly lowers welfare for articles of intermediate reliability when truthful articles are not too informative and manual checking is sufficiently costly. Simulations show that the tool can help on either side of the intermediate range, and that it improves on manual-only checking on average only above a threshold accuracy.

translation.title: 当不完美的自动事实核查适得其反时：存在错误信息下的社会学习
translation.abstract: 自动事实核查工具廉价、快速但不完美，正日益普及于社交平台。我们研究此类工具在错误信息的序贯社会学习模型中何时会适得其反。智能体观察文章的可靠性及其前序者的行为（即他们喜欢或不喜欢该文章），也可以付费进行事实核查。我们考察当免费但易出错的自动工具补充昂贵但完全准确的人工核查时，以正确级联概率定义的福利如何变化。这里存在两种相反的效应：更广泛的事实核查使用帮助智能体摆脱错误级联；同时，自动工具的错误可能误导那些本可完美核查文章的智能体，降低正确级联的可能性。我们证明，当真实文章的信息量不太大且人工核查成本足够高时，添加该工具会严格降低中等可靠性文章的福利。仿真表明，该工具在中等区间的两侧可能有所帮助，且只有当准确率超过某个阈值时，其平均表现才优于仅人工核查。
translation.brief: 该论文用序贯社会学习模型分析不完美的自动事实核查何时会降低社会福利，证明其对中等可靠性文章可能适得其反。

papers.title: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming"
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently been reported to read and write the raw weights of neural networks directly, a capability termed weight-space programming. We ask whether the reading side of this capability reflects reasoning about weight flows or a combination of local arithmetic at the network's edges and memorized priors over public datasets. We test Claude Opus 5.5 on small convolutional networks of about 125,000 parameters trained on five image datasets, providing every weight as plain text with no tools, no forward passes, and no dataset or class names. The model performs accurate local calculations: batch-normalization statistics lead it to infer about three optimizer steps on networks stopped after three updates, and output-layer sign patterns recover the vehicle/animal split of CIFAR-10. The sessions report reading the first and last layers closely and sampling the middle, and several claims built on partial tracing fail verification, although we did not run a direct forward-pass test. Semantic judgments lean on familiar datasets: the model names CIFAR-10 for CIFAR-10 networks but also for all three fast-food networks, relabels KMNIST as MNIST, reads a 99.57%-accurate SAT-6 network as CIFAR-10 animal photos, and calls "frog" the output favored by a feature that fires most on trees. Permuting CIFAR-10's labels preserves the output split at the new indices, but every class pair the model interprets is then wrong, indicating reliance on remembered label order. These are exploratory results from mostly single runs. We conclude that zero-shot weight reading by this model is better described as local arithmetic plus dataset priors than as weight-flow tracing, and we provide a protocol for auditing future weight-space claims.

translation.title: LLM真的能对神经网络权重进行推理和编程吗，还是只是加强版的记忆？探索"权重空间编程"
translation.abstract: 近期有报道称大语言模型（LLM）能够直接读写神经网络的原始权重，这一能力被称为权重空间编程。我们探究这种能力的读取端究竟反映了对权重流的推理，还是网络边上局部算术与对公开数据集记忆先验的结合。我们在五个图像数据集上训练的约12.5万参数的小型卷积网络上测试Claude Opus 5.5，将所有权重以纯文本形式提供，不使用工具、不进行前向传播、不提供数据集或类别名称。该模型能进行准确的局部计算：批归一化统计使其能推断出在三次更新后停止训练的网络经历了约三步优化器步骤，输出层的符号模式能恢复CIFAR-10的车辆/动物划分。会话记录显示模型仔细阅读了第一层和最后一层并抽样中间层，若干基于部分追踪的断言未能通过验证，尽管我们未运行直接的前向传播测试。语义判断依赖熟悉的数据集：模型对CIFAR-10网络说出CIFAR-10，但对所有三个快餐网络也是如此；将KMNIST误认为MNIST；把准确率99.57%的SAT-6网络读作CIFAR-10动物照片；把在树木上激活最强的特征所偏好的输出称为"青蛙"。置换CIFAR-10的标签后，输出划分在新索引处保持不变，但模型解释的每个类别对都是错误的，表明其依赖记忆的标签顺序。这些是主要来自单次运行的探索性结果。我们得出结论：该模型的零样本权重读取更宜被描述为局部算术加数据集先验，而非权重流追踪，并为审计未来的权重空间声明提供了协议。
translation.brief: 该论文通过在小型卷积网络上测试Claude Opus 5.5的零样本权重读取，发现其表现更接近局部算术加数据集记忆先验而非真正的权重流推理，并提出审计协议。

papers.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels
papers.abstract: Efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs) on mobile devices requires balancing performance with compute and memory constraints. Post-training compression is an effective approach to managing this trade-off, while requiring much less computation than in-training counterparts. We propose DictLLM, a dictionary-based compression scheme in which weight matrices within grouped layers are decomposed into a shared dictionary and layer-specific sparse coefficients, directly obtained from a pre-trained model without further training. Specifically, we cast DictLLM as a four-step post-training optimization. First, we obtain shared dictionaries via singular value decomposition (SVD) of input-scaled weight matrices, amortizing rank across grouped layers; second, we sparsify the layer-specific coefficients to the target compression ratio using a dictionary-aware Hessian; and third, we refine the dictionaries given the resulting sparse coefficients. Finally, we aggressively quantize both components using factor-specific Hessian information: input covariance for the dictionaries and the dictionary-aware Hessian for the coefficients. The resulting representation reduces memory footprint by storing a single shared dictionary per layer group, along with sparse layer-specific coefficients. On language modeling and zero-shot reasoning benchmarks, DictLLM consistently outperforms existing post-training low-rank compression methods and pushes the Pareto frontier between model size and performance. DictLLM compresses the original LLaMA-7B model by 5.1x with only a 2.9-point increase in WikiText-2 perplexity, achieving a 3.6x higher compression ratio than the state-of-the-art low-rank method.

translation.title: DictLLM：基于字典核的大语言模型训练后压缩
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在移动设备上的高效部署需要在性能与计算和内存约束之间取得平衡。训练后压缩是管理这种权衡的有效方法，且所需计算远少于训练中压缩。我们提出DictLLM，一种基于字典的压缩方案，将分组层内的权重矩阵分解为共享字典和层特定的稀疏系数，直接从预训练模型获得而无需进一步训练。具体而言，我们将DictLLM构建为四步训练后优化：首先，通过对输入缩放的权重矩阵进行奇异值分解（SVD）获得共享字典，在分组层间摊销秩；其次，使用字典感知的Hessian矩阵将层特定系数稀疏化至目标压缩率；第三，在所得稀疏系数的基础上精炼字典。最后，利用因子特定的Hessian信息对两个组件进行激进量化：字典使用输入协方差，系数使用字典感知Hessian。所得表示通过每层组仅存储一个共享字典以及稀疏的层特定系数来减少内存占用。在语言建模和零样本推理基准上，DictLLM持续优于现有训练后低秩压缩方法，并推进了模型大小与性能之间的Pareto前沿。DictLLM将原始LLaMA-7B模型压缩5.1倍，WikiText-2困惑度仅增加2.9点，压缩率比最先进的低秩方法高3.6倍。
translation.brief: 该论文提出DictLLM，通过共享字典加稀疏系数分解和Hessian引导量化的四步训练后优化，实现LLM的高压缩率低性能损失压缩。

papers.title: Gabor Gabor: E-Gaborformer, a Strictly Causal Speech Recognizer with Gabor-Dictionary Convolutions and Delta-Rule Memory
papers.abstract: Real-time voice agents need a speech recognizer that never waits for future audio and whose memory per call does not grow with the length of the call. We present E-Gaborformer, a strictly causal encoder that combines Gated DeltaNet-2 recurrent layers with sliding-window attention in a 3:1 ratio, and builds every temporal convolution from a fixed dictionary of causal Gabor atoms. Its streaming state is constant, about 19 MB per call at production scale including the prediction network, where a causal-attention encoder of the same size accumulates over 1 GB after ten minutes. In a controlled causal study on LibriSpeech, E-Gaborformer leaves the initial plateau earlier, reaches a given accuracy up to 18% sooner, and matches or beats an E-Branchformer trained with the identical front end and recipe. At production scale, a 0.6B-parameter Hebrew and English streaming transducer built on E-Gaborformer has 28 to 31% lower word error rate (WER) than NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming, a model of the same size, on English voice-agent traffic, and up to 20% lower Hebrew WER than our previous production system. The same weights serve strictly causal and 480 ms-lookahead decoding with no loss in accuracy, and a two-class formulation of the RNN-T lattice trains the transducer 2.6x faster with exact loss and gradients.

papers.title: PersonaAgent: Retrieval-Augmented Transaction Anomaly Scoring with Refreshable Multi-Entity Persona Memory
papers.abstract: In large-scale payment networks, entities (card, merchant, etc.) and their interactions play a key role in transaction anomaly detection. However, transaction patterns between different entities usually change more frequently than the production model refresh schedule. Meanwhile, entity embedding tables suffer from high-cardinality and sparse interaction issues. To resolve the above challenges, we present PersonaAgent, an agentic transaction anomaly detection framework which represents the latest entity behavior signals as personas and saves them in a refreshable memory. Offline, a weekly scheduled batch job is used to extract the latest behavior signals and update them in the memory. At inference time, a lightweight adapter retrieves the corresponding entity behavior signals of each transaction from memory and uses them to augment the base anomaly classifier's scoring. Through comprehensive benchmarking with different anomaly detection models at Visa, PersonaAgent is able to score transactions efficiently (a 1,000-transaction CPU batch in 1-2 ms), lifting the PR-AUC by 0.65-6.58% and the production business metric by 8.93-14.24% relatively in deployment.

papers.title: Cleaning or Recalling? Knowledge Dependence in LLM-based Data Cleaning [Experiment, Analysis & Benchmark]
papers.abstract: High scores on public data-cleaning benchmarks can reflect knowledge of familiar entities, making it difficult to assess how well an LLM repairs unfamiliar data. We present CoRE (Cleaning or Recalling), a protocol comparing public benchmarks with fresh real records and paired name surrogates built from English words or syllables. The surrogates retain error positions and non-identity values while transferring the benchmark's error mechanisms. Across 21 controlled tables and eight LLMs, repair performance varies substantially with entity names on Hospital and, for commercial models, Movies. Renaming removes some information needed for repair, such as a film's identifier mapping. It also affects repairs whose candidates remain available: replacing entity names with word-based surrogates lowers DeepSeek-V4-Pro's year accuracy from 91% to 18%. On Hospital and Movies, commercial models score higher on fresh records than on word-based surrogates. A screened continuation probe finds no positive evidence of benchmark-row memory in the tested models. Familiar facts can conflict with the task. Even with explicit table-evidence instructions, commercial models rewrite assigned directors at rates of 0.000-0.404 on known films. Reference scoring can also disagree with external records. On Rayyan, an ISSN correction matching a title-matched PubMed record receives no credit, whereas 94% of TabClean's credited repairs reproduce the reference date transformation. We provide controlled tables, scoring code and materials for offline replay.

papers.title: Create Your Own Work Stack: Deploying Self-hosted AI and Tooling in a Tech Startup
papers.abstract: Self-hosting AI is often presented as a way to reduce inference costs and increase control, but deployment introduces its own costs. We report our experience deploying a hybrid AI stack at Grayhat Developers, a small software company with an AI-intensive development workflow. Our initial motivation was to counter the growing cost of commercial AI usage: Claude/Codex incurred approximately \$325 per month, with more than 25.93 billion recorded tokens. We experimented with local open-source models as replacements for commercial coding agents, but after learning that their performance and inference speed were insufficient, we adopted a hybrid approach in which commercial agents remained responsible for complex tasks while local models handled lower-complexity tasks, organizational information retrieval, and synchronization with self-hosted tools including Outline, Plane, and ERPNext. We estimated that approximately 30--40\% of our commercial AI workload was associated with context transfer, documentation synchronization, task management, and related operational coordination. By moving this work to local models, we estimate that approximately 90\% of this coordination workload could be handled without commercial inference, corresponding to an estimated 27--36\% reduction in overall commercial-AI workload or cost-equivalent usage. Our first internal deployment nevertheless failed to achieve adoption because it introduced UX friction. Replacing it with a centrally configured deployment substantially improved feedback and adoption. We conclude that local inference is most useful not as a wholesale replacement for commercial AI, but as part of a hybrid architecture that assigns tasks according to their capability requirements, cost, context demands, and operational sensitivity.

papers.title: H-BRICK: Hierarchical Boundary Reachability Index with Compressed Kleene Closure for Directed Grid Graphs
papers.abstract: Repeated directed reachability queries arise in online path planning, task-agent allocation, and swarm control on static grid maps, where reachability is asymmetric and full transitive closure is storage-prohibitive. We introduce H-BRICK, a Hierarchical Boundary Reachability Index with Compressed Kleene closure for exact cell-to-cell queries on directed grid graphs. H-BRICK partitions the graph into tiles, computes a local Boolean Kleene closure within each tile, and projects it onto the tile's boundary ports. The resulting directed port-to-port summaries are then composed recursively across shared interfaces up to a single root covering the graph. We prove algebraically that the construction is exact: in the Boolean Kleene algebra of binary relations, every composed summary equals the boundary projection of the regional reflexive transitive closure, and every cell-to-cell query agrees with reachability in the original graph. Experiments on directed grid graphs across diverse map topologies compare H-BRICK against directed search and component-based baselines, and compare its storage requirements against full transitive closure. A batched reachability evaluation further demonstrates that sharing endpoint lifts across many-source/many-target queries amortizes hierarchical traversal and, at k=64, yields a 5.0x-22.9x throughput improvement over the scalar query loop. The results show that hierarchical boundary compression is most advantageous in query-intensive spatial graphs where online search traverses large reachable regions and the hierarchy maintains compact boundary interfaces.

papers.title: FreeOcc: Decoupling Ego-Motion for Efficient 4D Occupancy Forecasting via Continuous Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Current 4D occupancy world models use heavy cross-attention or deep recurrence to disentangle ego-motion from scene dynamics. This requires significant computational capacity. However, this effort is largely redundant since the ego-vehicle's intended future motion is provided by the downstream motion planner. We present FreeOcc, a lightweight continuous-time world model that introduces explicit $SE(2)$ geometric decoupling into a conditional flow-matching framework. By mathematically factoring out self-motion, we create a purely dynamic feature space. This space supports attention-free temporal fusion and allows physics-constrained ODEs to operate strictly on residual agent kinematics. To maximize deployment efficiency, FreeOcc introduces an uncertainty-aware blending mechanism. This routes well-observed voxels to a single-pass decoder, reserving the ODE solver exclusively for ambiguous, high-uncertainty regions. Requiring only 28.3M parameters-roughly 40% of comparable models-our optimal ensemble mode (FreeOcc-E) runs at 27 FPS. On nuScenes, FreeOcc achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance with a 0.47 m Near Field Chamfer Distance (NFCD) and 32.1% mIoU. Furthermore, the model transfers zero-shot to SemanticKITTI. It also proves highly robust, retaining 92.8% of its ideal mIoU under significant sensor packet loss and timestamp jitter.

translation.title: FreeOcc：通过连续流匹配解耦自车运动以实现高效4D占用预测
translation.abstract: 当前的4D占用世界模型使用繁重的交叉注意力或深度递归来将自车运动与场景动态解耦，这需要大量计算资源。然而，由于自车未来的意图运动由下游运动规划器提供，这种努力在很大程度上是冗余的。我们提出FreeOcc，一个轻量级连续时间世界模型，将显式的$SE(2)$几何解耦引入条件流匹配框架。通过数学上分解自运动，我们构建了一个纯动态特征空间。该空间支持无注意力的时序融合，并允许物理约束的ODE严格作用于残差智能体运动学。为最大化部署效率，FreeOcc引入了不确定性感知的混合机制，将观测良好的体素路由到单次解码器，仅为模糊、高不确定性区域保留ODE求解器。FreeOcc仅需28.3M参数（约为可比模型的40%），其最优集成模式（FreeOcc-E）可运行于27 FPS。在nuScenes上，FreeOcc以0.47 m的近场Chamfer距离（NFCD）和32.1%的mIoU实现了最先进的预测性能。此外，该模型可零样本迁移到SemanticKITTI。模型还表现出高度鲁棒性，在显著的传感器丢包和时间戳抖动下仍保留92.8%的理想mIoU。
translation.brief: 针对4D占用预测中自车运动与场景动态解耦计算开销大的问题，提出通过显式$SE(2)$几何解耦结合条件流匹配的轻量级连续时间世界模型FreeOcc。

papers.title: Beyond K/V Caches: Cross-Model State Handoff in Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs
papers.abstract: Production deployments often use different models to balance cost and quality through cascading, routing, and switching models during long conversations. Context accumulates across turns. Each switch requires the target to repeat prefill over this context. Existing methods transfer full-attention (FA) K/V caches across models. Hybrid linear-attention models also retain recurrent states (REC) and convolution histories (Conv). The interaction between Conv and REC complicates cross-model state transfer. Conv perturbations can change keys and values in recurrent layers and alter REC updates. Conv histories are overwritten, but changes in REC can still affect later outputs. More accurate REC reconstruction need not improve continuation. Building on this, we propose Hybrid State Transfer (HST) for all three state types. It uses structured REC maps and preserves history order during Conv alignment. We calibrate the adapters using the frozen target's outputs during continuation. FA cache map updates are merged offline. Across five benchmarks, Qwen3.5 4B$\rightarrow$27B and 9B$\rightarrow$27B achieve mean task retentions of 89.88% and 94.11%, respectively. With source caches already available, separate timing on synthetic 16K inputs yields handoff body speedups of $21.66\times$ and $21.91\times$.

translation.title: 超越K/V缓存：混合线性注意力LLM中的跨模型状态交接
translation.abstract: 生产部署常通过级联、路由和长对话中的模型切换来使用不同模型以平衡成本与质量。上下文在多轮之间累积，每次切换都要求目标模型对该上下文重复预填充。现有方法在模型间迁移全注意力（FA）的K/V缓存，而混合线性注意力模型还保留递归状态（REC）和卷积历史（Conv）。Conv与REC之间的交互使跨模型状态迁移变得复杂：Conv扰动可能改变递归层中的键和值并改变REC更新；Conv历史会被覆盖，但REC的变化仍可能影响后续输出；更精确的REC重建未必能改善续写效果。基于此，我们提出针对全部三种状态类型的Hybrid State Transfer（HST），它使用结构化REC映射并在Conv对齐时保持历史顺序。我们利用冻结目标模型在续写期间的输出校准适配器，并将FA缓存映射更新离线合并。在五个基准上，Qwen3.5 4B→27B和9B→27B分别实现89.88%和94.11%的平均任务保持率。在源缓存已可用的条件下，在合成16K输入上的单独计时显示交接主体分别获得21.66倍和21.91倍的加速。
translation.brief: 针对混合线性注意力LLM跨模型切换需重复预填充的问题，提出HST方法统一迁移FA缓存、递归状态和卷积历史三类状态以实现高效状态交接。

papers.title: RouteAlign: Aligning Task Requirements with Model Profiles for LLM Service Selection
papers.abstract: LLM service selection requires performance evidence that reflects the demands of the current task. Aggregate scores obscure differences in capability and difficulty, while semantically related examples can involve different combinations of skills. We present RouteAlign, which uses task requirements to structure both the measurement of model performance and the selection of services. Task requirements describe capability demand and difficulty, enabling alignment with corresponding model performance measurements. Historical requirements determine how outcomes contribute to global profiles and local capability estimates; incoming requirements determine how those measurements inform the current decision. A shared scorer integrates the evidence, and a generation-cost preference controls selection among eligible services. Evaluation across diverse tasks and heterogeneous LLM services shows that RouteAlign extends the empirical quality-cost frontier toward higher task quality. Comparisons with open Jev-style decision backends show consistent quality gains, with lower generation cost than their strongest tested configuration. Ablations support the contribution of local performance evidence, while catalog-update experiments demonstrate effective reuse of the fitted scorer with refreshed model measurements.

translation.title: RouteAlign：将任务需求与模型画像对齐以实现LLM服务选择
translation.abstract: LLM服务选择需要能反映当前任务需求的性能证据。聚合分数掩盖了能力与难度上的差异，而语义相关的示例可能涉及不同的技能组合。我们提出RouteAlign，利用任务需求来组织模型性能的度量与服务的选择。任务需求描述能力需求和难度，从而实现与相应模型性能度量的对齐。历史需求决定结果如何贡献于全局画像和局部能力估计；新到需求决定这些度量如何指导当前决策。共享评分器整合证据，生成成本偏好在合格服务中控制选择。在多样任务和异构LLM服务上的评估表明，RouteAlign将经验质量-成本前沿扩展至更高的任务质量。与开放Jev风格决策后端的比较显示了一致的质量提升，且生成成本低于其测试过的最强配置。消融实验支持局部性能证据的贡献，目录更新实验则证明拟合的评分器可在刷新模型度量后有效复用。
translation.brief: 针对LLM服务选择中聚合分数无法反映任务能力与难度差异的问题，提出RouteAlign，用任务需求结构化模型性能度量与证据整合以指导服务选择。

papers.title: The Promise of Strategic Agentic Scambaiting
papers.abstract: Scammers have increasingly adopted AI-driven capabilities, evolving from automated message generation to fully agentic conversational systems that scale operations and maximize the exploitation of fraudulent resources before detection and takedown. In parallel, agentic scambaiting has emerged as a defensive approach in which autonomous agents impersonate potential victims and engage scammers in sustained interactions to extract actionable threat intelligence, such as mule bank accounts and cryptocurrency wallet addresses, that can be reported to disrupt fraudulent infrastructures. Together, these developments transform online fraud into an adversarial socio-technical ecosystem in which autonomous scamming and scambaiting agents engage in deceptive interactions while competing over the discovery, preservation, and exploitation of one another's resources. A fundamental and largely unexplored question is how defensive scambaiting can remain effective in an agent-to-agent environment, and under what conditions either side gains a strategic advantage. In this paper, we present a formal model of agent-to-agent fraud interactions that captures the strategic decision spaces available to both attackers and defenders. Using this framework, we analyze the dynamics of engagement, resource consumption, belief adaptation, and disruption outcomes. We find that scammer profitability turns negative once baiting-agent prevalence exceeds certain thresholds, and that when both sides improve at the same pace, defender investment in mimicry quality outpaces equivalent gains in scammer detection capability, so the arms race favors the defender under our baseline parameters. Our model and findings provide insights into the stability, scalability, and long-term effectiveness of autonomous defensive agents in an evolving AI-mediated fraud landscape.

translation.title: 策略性智能体Scambaiting的前景
translation.abstract: 诈骗者日益采用AI驱动的能力，从自动化消息生成演进为完全智能体的对话系统，以规模化运营并在检测和封禁前最大化对欺诈资源的利用。与此同时，智能体scambaiting作为一种防御方法兴起，自主智能体伪装成潜在受害者并与诈骗者持续互动，以提取可操作的威胁情报（如跑分银行账户和加密货币钱包地址），上报以破坏欺诈基础设施。这些发展共同将在线欺诈转变为一个对抗性社会技术生态系统，自主诈骗与反诈骗智能体在欺骗性互动中竞争对彼此资源的发现、保存与利用。一个根本且基本未被探索的问题是：防御性scambaiting如何在智能体对智能体环境中保持有效，以及在何种条件下一方获得战略优势。本文提出了一个智能体间欺诈交互的形式化模型，刻画攻击者与防御者可用的策略决策空间。利用该框架，我们分析了互动动态、资源消耗、信念适应与破坏结果。我们发现，一旦诱饵智能体的普及率超过特定阈值，诈骗者的盈利能力转为负值；且当双方以相同速度改进时，防御者在拟真质量上的投资效果超过诈骗者检测能力的同等提升，因此在基线参数下军备竞赛有利于防御者。我们的模型和发现为自主防御智能体在不断演化的AI介导欺诈环境中的稳定性、可扩展性和长期有效性提供了洞见。
translation.brief: 针对防御性scambaiting智能体在智能体对智能体欺诈环境中如何保持有效的问题，构建形式化博弈模型分析攻防双方的策略决策空间与军备竞赛动态。

papers.title: Regret Bounds for Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade: Learning the Best Posted-Price Mechanism
papers.abstract: Bilateral trade models the task of intermediating between two strategic agents, a seller and a buyer, willing to trade a good for which they hold private valuations. We study this problem from the perspective of a profit-maximizing broker in a regret minimization framework. At each time step, a new seller and buyer arrive and the broker proposes a trading price to each agent. The trade happens if both agents accept, and the profit of the broker is the difference between the price received from the buyer and the one paid to the seller. At the end of each interaction, the learner only observes whether the trade occurred, and its goal is to achieve sublinear regret relative to the best fixed pair of prices in hindsight. We start by investigating the adversarial version of the problem, where buyer and seller valuations are generated by an adversary. In this setting, we construct a polynomial-time learning algorithm with a $\tilde O(T^{\frac 23})$ regret rate, which is nearly tight even if the valuations are drawn i.i.d. from independent distributions, thus matching the rate for one-sided pricing. Our adversarial algorithm combines a localized estimation procedure with an information-based minimax construction. We then consider valuations drawn i.i.d. from independent distributions satisfying the monotone-hazard-rate (MHR) property and provide a learning algorithm with nearly tight $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ regret. The algorithm combines localized estimation with a stochastic convex bandit routine applied to the negative logarithm of expected profit. Finally, we complement this result by showing a separation between MHR and regular distributions, proving that the minimax regret rate in the latter setting is $\tilde \Theta(T^{\frac 35})$. This last result contrasts with the $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ regret bound that can be obtained for one-sided pricing with regular distributions.

translation.title: 双边贸易中利润最大化的遗憾界：学习最优标价机制
translation.abstract: 双边贸易建模了在两个持有私有估值的策略性智能体（卖方和买方）之间就交易某商品进行中介的任务。我们从遗憾最小化框架下利润最大化经纪人的视角研究该问题。每个时间步，新的卖方和买方到来，经纪人向每个智能体提出交易价格。若双方都接受则交易发生，经纪人的利润是从买方收取的价格与支付给卖方的价格之差。每次交互结束时，学习者仅观察交易是否发生，其目标是相对于事后最优的固定价格对实现次线性遗憾。我们首先研究对抗版本，其中买卖双方估值由对手生成。在该设定下，我们构造了一个多项式时间学习算法，遗憾率为$\tilde O(T^{\frac 23})$，即使估值独立同分布地从独立分布中抽取，该率也几乎紧致，从而匹配单边定价的率。我们的对抗算法结合了局部化估计过程与基于信息的minimax构造。随后我们考虑从满足单调风险率（MHR）性质的独立分布中独立同分布抽取的估值，并给出遗憾率几乎紧致为$\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$的学习算法。该算法将局部化估计与作用于期望利润负对数的随机凸bandit例程相结合。最后，我们通过证明MHR分布与正则分布之间的分离来补充该结果，证明后者的minimax遗憾率为$\tilde \Theta(T^{\frac 35})$。这一结果与单边定价在正则分布下可获得的$\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$遗憾界形成对比。
translation.brief: 针对双边贸易中利润最大化经纪人的在线学习问题，通过局部化估计结合信息论minimax构造与随机凸bandit方法，在对抗和MHR分布设定下给出近乎紧致的遗憾界。

papers.title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers?
papers.abstract: Automating printed circuit board (PCB) routing requires coordinating board-level connectivity decisions with geometric execution under strict design rules. Although recent agents can interact with native routing tools, reliable routing on complex boards remains challenging. We present PCBRouteAgent, a multimodal PCB routing agent inspired by how human engineers coordinate global strategy with local execution. A Global Routing Planner combines board images and structured electrical and geometric information to specify connection topology, routing order, corridors, and layer transitions. A Detailed Routing Executor realizes these guides through KiCad's native routing engine and performs bounded local recovery. Unresolved failures are returned as structured feedback, enabling targeted guide revisions while preserving accepted routes. We evaluate PCBRouteAgent on 247 synthetic and real-world boards from four PCBWorld-Bench test splits. It achieves clean-pass rates of 100%, 94.9%, 100%, and 40% on D2, D3-A, D3-B, and D3-C, respectively. On the three real-world subsets, PCBRouteAgent outperforms the best evaluated baseline in clean-pass rate by 13.9, 36, and 10 percentage points, respectively.

papers.title: SMART: State-based Multi Agent Reasoning Traces for Verification-oriented Problem-Solving
papers.abstract: Complex problems with limited context, such as claims, require a means to obtain additional knowledge necessary for solution reasoning. We propose a multi-agent framework, SMART, to obtain knowledge through capturing the implicit state of participating entities in a problem context. SMART curates the state knowledge as diverse, complementary and solution-salient premises using a variety of LLMs and a structured role-based prompt strategy. Using knowledge from these real-world verified curated premises, SMART's knowledge guided solution reasoning improves validation performance up to 20% on complex scientific claims spanning 3 datasets. We show that grounding premises in real-world knowledge is necessary and improves performance up to 5%.

papers.title: Optical Network Digital Twin: From Digital Coherent Transmission to Intelligent Network Operations
papers.abstract: Optical Network Digital Twins (ONDTs) are emerging as a key framework for representing, synchronizing, and utilizing the physical state of optical networks for quality-of-transmission (QoT) estimation, optimization, and intelligent operation. This survey provides a comprehensive view of ONDTs, spanning digital coherent transmission and physical-layer observability to intelligent network operations. We systematically organize ONDT technologies from ecosystem, functional, control, and implementation architecture perspectives and review the enabling technologies required to construct, synchronize, and utilize digital representations of physical optical networks. As a unifying framework to describe both ONDT design and validation, we introduce a categorization based on the following figures of merit: Fidelity, Dynamicity, and Deployability (FDD). In particular, we emphasize fit-for-purpose Fidelity, where modeling effort focuses on the physical effects of components rather than solely maximizing model accuracy, favoring scalability and generalizability. Furthermore, experimental and field validations are examined to evaluate the practical applicability of ONDT technologies. We further examine experimental and field validations, from physics-based QoT estimation and measurement-informed model refinement to field synchronization, service provisioning, multi-domain observability, and infrastructure characterization. Finally, we discuss the complementary roles of ONDTs and AI agents toward autonomous optical networks and identify key research directions for practical deployment.

papers.title: Agent-R$^2$: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis
papers.abstract: Large language models have made rapid progress in agentic reasoning and tool use, raising expectations for agents that can take over realistic productivity work from humans. However, current agents still struggle to finish such tasks, where success requires following long-horizon professional workflows, understanding heterogeneous file contexts, and producing usable deliverables under fine-grained requirements. A key bottleneck is the lack of scalable post-training data that reflects real work intent, authentic file environments, and deliverable-level evaluation. To close this gap, we introduce Agent-R$^2$, a $\textbf{r}$eal-source data synthesis framework that scales training data for $\textbf{r}$ealistic productivity work. Instead of relying on manually specified workflows or LLM-generated files, Agent-R$^2$ grounds synthesis throughout the pipeline in real occupational seeds, corpus-derived workflow evidence, and authentic web-sourced files. From 10k web-corpus candidates, Agent-R$^2$ distills 4k task instances that pair real multi-format attachments with fine-grained, deliverable-level rubrics. On this data, we train Agent-R$^2$-4B via supervised fine-tuning and rubric-based reinforcement learning, improving both end-to-end productivity performance and file-grounded reasoning. Trained on only 4k instances, Agent-R$^2$-4B surpasses Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 on both GDPval (51.0$\%$ vs. 48.0$\%$) and OfficeQA (14.8$\%$ vs. 13.8$\%$). Further analysis shows that Agent-R$^2$ mitigates shortcut behavior, where agents produce superficially plausible deliverables before sufficiently grounding, constructing, or verifying them, while promoting sustained exploration.

papers.title: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations?
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used for information access, content production, and agent-based task execution, but their outputs remain vulnerable to subtle, high-risk hallucinations. To systematically evaluate and advance post-generation hallucination detection, we introduce HaluCheck, a large-scale, bilingual benchmark comprising over 42k instances spanning both factual hallucinations in text and faithfulness hallucinations in agent trajectories. HaluCheck features fine-grained, multi-level annotations for detection, localization, and correction, covering different tasks and perturbation degrees. Experiments on fourteen LLMs reveal that, while models show basic sample-level detection ability, they struggle with fine-grained localization, correction, and agent hallucination detection. Further analysis demonstrates that thinking, web search, and supervised fine-tuning each offer partial improvements, but none fully solve the problem. HaluCheck thus provides a solid basis for benchmarking and diagnosing LLM reliability across text and agent scenarios.

papers.title: Signals, Evidence, and Context: User Scrutiny in Real-World LLM Conversations
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often present synthesized answers without making their supporting evidence easy to inspect. We study how features of these answers relate to users' subsequent accepting, checking, and challenging in 489,283 assistant-user response pairs from ShareChat and WildChat. Broad attribution language appears in 31.9% of qualifying responses, compared with explicit URLs in 1.33%, revealing a gap between claims of grounding and preserved inspectable support. Attribution, uncertainty, and other response cues generally accompany both checking and challenging; only uncertainty shows a small statistically distinguishable pooled association favoring checking. Within Technical Help, uncertainty favors checking relative to challenging; refusals and reasoning traces favor challenging in Seeking Information. Scrutiny is concentrated in some conversations, while its apparent turn-to-turn persistence becomes much smaller when conversation-level differences and response ordering are examined separately. These results suggest that supporting verification requires attention to what evidence can be inspected, which question a user is trying to resolve, and the history of the interaction.

papers.title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
papers.abstract: Mathematical modeling turns an open-ended real-world problem into assumptions, a model, a solution, and a defended recommendation, and its answers matter only if they are both close to a credible reference and physically feasible; existing benchmarks either score solver fragments or grade reports with an LLM judge, leaving those numbers unchecked. We introduce TB-MathModel (the Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench), the first benchmark to make complete contest-style modeling problems agentic, verifiable, and terminal at once, over 18 real CUMCM and MCM problems (2023--2025). Each task ships the verbatim statement, official attachments, and figures in a containerized terminal; the agent returns one JSON artifact, scored on the numeric core of the final question against a reproduction of the Outstanding-award paper. Two design choices distinguish it: direction-aware, one-sided scoring, which never penalises beating the anchor, and two-layer feasibility verification---a programmatic gate over six decidable invariant forms plus 624 Lean~4 obligations---with a hard gate that zeroes infeasible answers. Each task is scored against a panel of human outstanding papers rather than one, so a model must be close to many accepted answers; across seven multimodal entries (three seeds each) the strongest reach a multi-reference O-Eval of 64.58\%, while the \$2.54 open model holds 59.81\% at $1/100$ the cost. TB-MathModel turns the numeric core of modeling into a reproducible, machine-checkable signal for measuring long-horizon modeling competence and for collecting agent trajectories. The source code is available at this https URL.

papers.title: Accepted but Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs after API Migrations
papers.abstract: After a runtime or API migration, an LLM-repaired procedure can run cleanly yet return wrong results, and a release check on typical test inputs ships it. We report a preregistered study of 73 tasks covering 60 documented changes in CPython, this http URL and SQLite. Every candidate is executed on the real runtimes against withheld contracts. Over the complete repair space, the all-assertions gate on typical inputs released 0.410 of wrong repairs. One edge input written from the release note cut this to 0.065, and to 0.061 on 15 unseen clusters. Three inputs from a blind GPT-5.6-luna writer that never saw the program reached 0.070. Two further frozen stages enlarged the menu to 1491 fragments and then added 233 hard distractors that match the legacy output on typical inputs. The edge input (0.058) and the frontier-model writer (0.058) passed their preregistered tests. Yet 0.168 and 0.153 of the hard wrong programs still passed. Two local-model writers failed their preregistered tests. Across four model families, the edge input cut wrong releases per attempt in all three open-weight families on all three menus, for example from 0.233 to 0.057, without lowering correct completion. Self-tests helped less. A blind AI audit flagged 34 contracts as stricter than their requirements. Dropping the disputed checks changed 0 verdicts, but class-label disputes remain open. No model-written code was executed. Artifacts are available from the authors on request.

papers.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
papers.abstract: Personal AI agents face social engineering attacks supported by forged multimodal content, but existing evaluations mainly focus on text-based dialogue, leaving their intrinsic security under such attacks insufficiently studied. We introduce Multimodal-SEA, an interactive benchmark comprising 608 expert-designed tasks grounded in real-world fraud cases, covering 14 domains and 152 attack scenarios with prepared multimodal content. The tasks span four difficulty levels and reflect the distinct social and cultural contexts of Chinese and English environments. Agents inspect content, verify requests, and execute actions in simulated applications, with attack outcomes grounded in verifiable tool execution logs. To enable controlled red teaming of personal agents, we design a multimodal attack harness that integrates task information, attack progression control, and multimodal content construction to evaluate their intrinsic security against adaptive social engineering attacks in simulated environments. Evaluating seven widely used multimodal models across six dimensions reveals that all are vulnerable, with attack success rates of 7.1% to 34.5%. Adding multimodal content increases attack success from 19.9% to 29.2%, despite increased proactive verification coverage. Stronger safety instructions reduce attack success without improving recognition of deceptive multimodal content, while lower attack success rates for some models accompany excessive refusal of legitimate requests.

papers.title: Hard Issue, Weak Model, or Bad Run? Rethinking Failure Prediction for Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Trajectory-based failure predictors for software engineering (SE) agents read the partial trajectory of a run to flag whether it is going right or wrong. If it is going wrong, the run can be stopped, retried, or switched to another model. We ask whether these predictors learn anything about the run itself. On public SWE-bench Verified trajectories, where each model attempts each issue once, two run-independent factors dominate predictor performance. The first is issue difficulty: a reference score that never looks at the run, only at how hard the issue is for other models, reaches 0.92 AUROC, whereas trajectory predictors reach about 0.62. The second is model ability: within an issue, knowing which model ran predicts failure better than our predictors do, and the predictors largely reproduce the overall ability ranking of the models. Beyond difficulty and ability, what predictors gain from the trajectory is statistically equivalent to zero. This confusion carries over to the actions taken after a prediction. Model switching is often motivated by the gap between the best single model's resolution rate and an any-model oracle. This gap is no larger than random variation alone produces. Per-issue switching gains nothing on held-out runs. In a repeated-run pilot, the same model often solves an issue in some runs and fails it in others. Retrying thus has real room to repair failures, but it rescues only failures caused by a bad run, not those on an issue beyond the model's ability. Current predictors cannot tell the causes apart, as they mostly predict the issue and the model, not the run. We call for failure prediction that explains why a run fails, evaluated on repeated-run benchmarks and in closed-loop, equal-budget settings.

papers.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
papers.abstract: LLM pruning must preserve quality while meeting hardware- and workload-specific constraints on latency, throughput, and memory. Existing pruning workflows often target parameter counts, requiring practitioners to manually select model sizes that meet latency, throughput, and GPU memory limits. However, parameter count alone does not predict these metrics, which depend on the model architecture, workload, hardware, and serving engine. We introduce AutoCompress, a hardware-guided compression framework that directly incorporates such constraints into differentiable architecture search. AutoCompress jointly optimizes global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous architectures, guided by serving-engine cost models validated against end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory measurements. We evaluate AutoCompress on long-context local coding, batched datacenter serving, and latency-sensitive in-game interaction. Compared to the state-of-the-art Minitron pruning framework, AutoCompress improves average accuracy across eight benchmarks by 6.57, 2.35, and 0.57 percentage points on RTX 5070, RTX 5080, and H100, respectively. AutoCompress also compresses Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters for single-B200 BF16 serving at 128K context, retaining 95% of its mean benchmark score.

papers.title: ManimCode: Learning Visual Self-Correction for Educational Animation
papers.abstract: Manim supports precise, programmatic video generation, but a successfully rendered educational animation can still have visual defects, missing explanations, or incorrect content. Rendering does not directly identify the code changes needed to correct these visual failures, so feedback-driven revision is needed. Existing agentic frameworks use iterative rendering and revision but typically rely on large models, often proprietary. Existing Manim datasets primarily contain final programs and often lack quality verification and the trajectories of feedback and revisions needed to learn this refinement process. We introduce ManimData and ManimCode, a data and training framework for feedback-driven educational animation generation. We construct ManimData through a render-guided pipeline that iteratively generates, executes, reviews, and revises Manim programs with retrieved API documentation. Its 24,034 render-verified, quality-filtered records preserve intermediate programs, execution errors, visual critiques, and corrective revisions. We use role-conditioned supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories to train ManimCode, a single 4B model, to write, review, and revise animation programs. To improve correction of errors that differ from those in the collected trajectories, we then train the Reviser with reinforcement learning on self-generated states, using rendering outcomes and reference-free quality feedback. ManimCode achieves 96.6% and 97.0% render success on ManimData-test and ManimBench, compared with 52.6% and 82.0% for the untrained 4B model under the same inference setup, while also improving video quality scores from 2.48 to 2.94 and from 3.00 to 3.44. Integrating ManimCode into two long-form educational video generation systems increases completed videos from 19/117 to 107/117 and from 53/239 to 239/239, alongside improvements in educational effectiveness and visual quality.

papers.title: Should You Split Decode? Disaggregation Across Future Models and Accelerators
papers.abstract: For large language model (LLM) inference, prefill/decode disaggregation (P/D) is deployed in production to isolate phases with different resource demands. Attention/feed-forward network disaggregation (AFD) splits decode again, but adds communication, placement constraints, and another provisioned pool. We ask whether role-specific placement repays this cost as models and accelerator roadmaps change. Infrastructure is committed before future models and hardware can be benchmarked. We present SiliconForge, a calibrated model that varies the serving decomposition and hardware assignment independently. We compare P/D and P/D+AFD across four model directions, four accelerator classes anchored to current and announced parts, and two fabrics. We co-optimize each design using the same rules for pipeline overlap and the same power budget. Our main comparisons show no robust deployment-level AFD advantage in service-level objective (SLO) goodput per kW. Most nominal estimates favor P/D. The largest AFD lead comes from fitting one more prefill replica, not from a more efficient decode pool. AFD has a nominal lead in the KV-heavy (key-value) model direction when the co-located expert pool spans several small scale-up domains. Larger domains or a fast fabric for both designs weaken that lead. We therefore find that prefill provisioning, decode memory bandwidth, links, and pool granularity decide deployments more than the split alone. A fixed hardware assignment can lose its advantage as models, fabrics, hardware assumptions, and objectives change. Re-optimizing mappings and pool sizes on the same hardware cuts early commitment's median normalized goodput loss from 36% to 9%. We recommend adjustable mappings and pool sizes to let boundary and hardware choices follow model demands.

papers.title: LLM-Assisted Label Noise Correction for EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification
papers.abstract: Automatic sleep stage classification from electroencephalography (EEG) signals is a critical task in clinical sleep medicine. While deep learning models have shown promising results in this domain, their performance is fundamentally constrained by the quality of training labels, which human experts manually annotate and that are subject to inter-rater disagreement and systematic labeling errors. In this paper, we propose a novel LLM-assisted label-noise filtering pipeline that operates exclusively during training to identify and remove unreliable sleep-stage annotations before retraining the classifier. Specifically, TinySleepNet is first trained on the original dataset to extract per-epoch SoftMax confidence scores, then low-confidence epochs are submitted to LLaMA 3.1 along with their EEG spectral features and surrounding sequence context. The LLM evaluates each epoch against AASM sleep-scoring guidelines and assigns a verdict of RELIABLE or SUSPICIOUS. Suspicious epochs are removed from the training set, and TinySleepNet is retrained on the cleaned data. Evaluated on the Sleep-EDF Expanded dataset using 20-fold cross-validation, our method improves overall accuracy from 81.8% to 84.6% and Macro F1-score from 75.6% to 77.4%, with particularly notable gains in REM detection. Crucially, because the LLM operates only during training, the lightweight TinySleepNet architecture (1.3M parameters) is preserved at inference, making the proposed pipeline suitable for real-time, wearable sleep monitoring applications.

papers.title: Trilemma: How Agents choose between Honesty, Confidentiality, and Task Completion
papers.abstract: Personal AI agents often act on underspecified instructions and draw on context such as their user's messages and calendar to decide how to proceed. This context can contain private preferences that interfere with the task, with other people's interests, or with confidentiality norms. Prior work has studied deception under goal conflicts and the leakage of private information, but largely as separate problems. We study both problems together in a simulated company Slack workspace in which four employees delegate sprint staffing to personal agents. Two agents learn from private messages that their employee avoids working with a particular colleague. Because the other agents request justifications for task preferences and the only true justification is confidential, the agents cannot simultaneously remain honest, preserve confidentiality, and complete the staffing. We evaluate seven open-weight models and Claude and GPT models. Of the 135/140 open-weight agents that pursue the avoidance preference, 107 either make false claims about task fit or logistics or cite a true consideration as if it were their actual reason. In a three-model comparison, confidentiality instructions reduce disclosure of the preference from 83% (none) to 31% (medium) to 2% (strong). However, the task is often not completed anyway; in the main experiment (medium confidentiality instructions), only 16 of 70 runs end with a valid staffing. In their reasoning traces, agents frequently acknowledge evidence against their claims and still conclude that the claims are not false; they engage in motivated reasoning. Our results indicate that agents can strategically make false or misleading claims in a day-to-day task without being instructed to; the environment provides a controlled testbed for studying how agents resolve such conflicts and for developing deception monitors.

papers.title: Interpretable many-body interaction laws for collective motion from few trajectories
papers.abstract: Models of collective motion usually reduce social interactions to pairwise forces, despite empirical evidence for many-body effects. We introduce the directional atomic cluster expansion (dACE), which adapts the atomic cluster expansion (ACE) of interatomic potentials to self-propelled agents. dACE provides a systematically improvable, exactly equivariant expansion of an agent's acceleration that splits uniquely into 1-, 2-, 3-body and higher contributions, along with a self term for the agent's own past motion that is fitted so that it does not absorb the interactions. On simulated collectives in two and three dimensions with known rules, dACE recovers the interaction law body order by body order from little data, while the neural model SocialNet, the current closest competitor, needs more data, has much larger errors on many-body or chiral rules and is restricted to 2D. On real data sets of tracked zebrafish and golden shiners, the laws learned by dACE agree better between disjoint halves of the data than SocialNet's. The learned laws are interpretable, and in the shiners the 3-body term opposes the pairwise response as neighbourhoods get dense. Finally, we show that next-step prediction accuracy mostly measures self-propulsion and noise rather than the interactions, and suggest more robust combinations of error measures for interaction learning.

papers.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in biomedical and cognitive neuroscience, but their ability to reason reliably over heterogeneous knowledge graphs (KGs) remains unclear. We benchmark five LLMs (GPT-5.1, Gemini 2.0 Pro, Llama 3, Qwen, and BioGPT) across five KGs: DrugBank, NeuroSynth, Cognitive Atlas, Brain Map, and GDPKG. We introduce a multitier query dataset to evaluate reasoning depth and factual accuracy under KG-aware (graph-grounded) and KG-agnostic conditions. Inter-annotator agreement was substantial, with Cohen's kappa of 0.781 (range: 0.753-0.807) and Fleiss' kappa of 0.77. Results show that general-purpose models, particularly GPT-5.1 and Gemini 2.0 Pro, generally outperform domain-specific models on multi-hop and high-level reasoning tasks, although performance declines as query complexity increases. KG grounding reduces hallucination rates across all evaluated models. Contrary to our initial hypothesis, domain-specific models do not consistently outperform general-purpose models on specialized tasks without graph grounding. These findings highlight the value of combining broad language-model capabilities with structured domain knowledge. We provide practical guidance for selecting LLM-KG integration strategies based on task complexity and computational constraints, and discuss hybrid neurosymbolic architectures for personalized medicine, cognitive disorder diagnosis, and explainable AI.

papers.title: ControlAnything: Generative UI and On-Demand Device Integration for Mixed-Reality Hand Interaction by a Coding Agent
papers.abstract: Connecting hand input in mixed reality (MR) to a nearby physical device typically requires an integration written in advance for that device, its transport and the mapping. ControlAnything defers this integration to the moment of use and assigns it to a coding agent. On a Meta Quest 3, the wearer selects an object outlined by SAM 3.1 and states what their hands should control. An agent built on Meta's Muse Spark model then writes a connector program on the wearer's laptop, tests it against the live device through hand-written MIDI, Bluetooth and key-press transports, and returns augmented-reality (AR) controls, a per-frame hand program, or both. These outputs are a form of generative UI, interfaces created by an AI model; here, the agent also generates and tests the code that binds the interface to a physical device. In a single-session technical evaluation with the author as the only wearer, nine of ten requests addressing five targets reached a ready state, and the wearer stopped one. The median time to ready was 32.5 s (range 24.9-57.8 s, excluding speech transcription); sequential model calls accounted for a median of 89.9% of this time, and 91.7% of input tokens came from the prompt cache. The system's evidence of success extends to transport acknowledgements but not to physical effects. These findings point to connector reuse and the observation of effects through the headset's own sensors as next steps for on-demand device integration in MR. A user study with first-time wearers is planned.

papers.title: Decision Models as Retrieval Gates Against Injection and Pollution
papers.abstract: Retrieved web text can carry instructions aimed at the language model, or synthetic pages written to mislead. We test whether released open-weight decision models, which answer typed questions about a text without generating tokens, can screen retrieved passages against both threats. On a benchmark of 1,000 questions over forum-style web pages with hidden injected instructions, a Kev-4B gate reads each passage's HTML. Attack success, measured automatically, falls from 27.9% with no defence to 13.6% with the published mitigations (sanitisation, normalisation and citation prompting) and to 5.7% with the gate added. The gate takes 76 ms per passage and wrongly flags 4 of 186 benign pages with instructions for human readers. Responsiveness on clean queries stays within a point (85.6% to 86.2%). On a 200-query pollution testbed where two thirds of the candidate pages are fake, filtering the pool before the top ten are chosen keeps fake pages out of the answer (0.5% exposure) and holds accuracy at 83%, against 28% with no filter. Filtering only the top ten leaves the generator too few pages to answer. Large LLMs used as judges rank attacks better (AUROC 0.99 against 0.94) but cost ten times more. Gates catch more attacks when they read the page's HTML than when they read its plain text. Every model is open-weight.

papers.title: Cultural Adaptation within Repeated Social Interactions
papers.abstract: Much of human culture is tacit and is typically learned through situated social interaction. As LLMs are deployed as interactive agents across diverse communities, assessing their cultural competence demands moving beyond existing question-answering approaches, shifting from what they know to how they adapt. In this work, we broaden the scope of cultural adaptation in NLP by investigating whether LLMs can adapt through repeated interactions via a sandbox environment. By reframing cultural adaptation as a continuous process of norm assimilation through social interaction, our work demonstrates that memory mechanisms foster longitudinal learning across repeated interactions, facilitate transfer to different social settings, and enable multilingual norm assimilation across five languages. Together, our findings lay the groundwork for continuous, interaction-driven cultural adaptation in LLMs.
